_source: L19 (work plan 2). More of the original's voice, never contradicting it and never a floor count. Built on its own phrases: the Chief's Hall inscription (MEASURE THE GRAIN. COUNT THE FLASKS. KEEP THE DOOR.), the architect and his toys, the bell with no clapper, the scar that misfires every spell, the dungeon still being built. Budget (origins.json): one 'tell' per delve, on its first floor.

lord_intros.hollow_king: The braziers in the hall burn blue, and then burn cold.
lord_intros.grubmother: The floor is wet, and getting wetter.
lord_intros.rattling_host: Somewhere ahead, something counts its own bones out loud.
lord_intros.nightwing: Every torch on the floor gutters at once.
lord_intros.gravewyrm: The dungeon was built around this, and it knows it.
lord_intros.ossuary_lord: It has waited a very long time. A little longer is nothing.
lord_intros.pale_duchess: A lady laughs somewhere ahead, very politely.
lord_intros.mourncoil: Breath steams. Then the steam freezes.

unique_intros.mother_silk: The threads across the doorway are new.

hollow_king: Blue light under the door, and no heat in it.
Something cold is already seated in the hall.

grubmother: The wet reaches the boots before the sound does.
The walls move, and it is not the walls.
Something is birthing in the dark ahead, and not stopping.

Something ahead is full and still feeding.

rattling_host: A hundred small knocks, all keeping time.

The floor lifts, very slightly, and settles.

'The door is kept. Say it back to me.'
'Breathe now - we will be busy later.'
'Nobody dies in the first room. It is rude.'
Scratch the turns as we take them.
lord: Hold the line, not the ground.
It carries a note. Make it short.
'That is the one the Chronicle names.'
'Let it be noted that I came anyway.'
Watch its feet, not its face.
It wants the door. Do not give it.
'It has one good trick. Make it use it.'
'If I fall, somebody finish the sentence.'
It's slow. Be slower than nothing.
This is what we came for.
That's the one from the tell.
Two on it, rest watch the room.
Hold the line, hold the door.
Make it come through the gap.
Last push or last stand - pick!
trap: Stand clear - I will tread it.
'That was a floor a moment ago.'
'The guild should chalk these. The guild should pay me to chalk these.'
Somebody counted these steps before us.
'Hold still and let me be clever.'
'The stone moved. Stone should not move.'
'That is a pit with a lid on it.'
There's a seam in the stone.
Hands where I can see them.
hurt: Hold the door, I will keep.
'That one is going in the Chronicle.'
Mend me, then shout at me.
Took it on the shield. Mostly.
I will walk. Watch me walk.
'That is coming out of somebody's share.'
'The door is still kept. So am I.'
Don't look at me, look at it!
Keep it off me a breath.
That one's going on the stone.
drink: That is the last of it.
'The apothecary counted this one out loud.'
Tastes like the slate at the apothecary.
Half a flask, half a man.
'The flask was counted. So am I.'
Back on my feet, back in it.

The scar's answering again.
Stupid scar.
The scar took it.
Wrong spell, wrong day.
It answered, not me.
Hate this ground.
Came out sideways.
Scar's greedy today.
Not what I asked for.
Every time, this floor.
The ground ate it.
Asked for fire. Got weather.
Scar's listening again.
Not my spell. Not my fault.
Scar had other plans.
That is not what I said.
Cast fire, got frost.
The ground is casting now.
Wild down here. Always.
Ask the scar, not me.
The words went somewhere else.
Nat one. Of course.
The scar is in a mood.
No spell survives this floor.
Wrong, and loudly wrong.
I will try again. Stand back.
'That is not what that does.'
'The scar had a better idea.'
'Nobody write that down.'
'It worked in the yard!'
Cast a ward, got a wind.
The floor is in a mood tonight.
That went backwards.
Wrong word, wrong floor.
'The scar finished my sentence.'
'I would like that one back.'
'Nobody tell the guild.'
'It is the ground. It is definitely the ground.'
Not what I asked for!
The scar's taking a cut.
Wrong spell, wrong room.
It went the other way!
That's on the ground, not me.
The scar heard me wrong.
I had it. The scar had it harder.
Again, and properly!
Ask the scar, not me.
That is NOT fire.
The scar had other plans.
That went somewhere else.
Wrong spell. Right scar.
It takes a toll. That was the toll.
I said fire. It heard something.
Give it back!
The scar's in a mood.
Not my aim. Its aim.
That one's the scar's, not mine.
I'll try again. Stand clear.
Hold still - that one bounced.
Every time, down here.

epitaphs: Measured the grain. Counted the flasks. Kept the door.
The scar keeps what it takes.
Went down with a lamp. Did not come up.
The guild writes the name and keeps it.
Somewhere below, a bell with no clapper rings once.
One floor too many.
Lit a lamp. The dark kept it.
Counted every flask but the last.
The guild writes the name; the scar keeps the rest.
Measured the grain. The grain ran out.
Went down proving something. Proved it.
Kept the door, until the door kept them.
The bell with no clapper rang, and they did not come up.
Named on the roll, and marked with a dagger.
Paid the guild's price in full.
The door held. They did not.
Last seen going down, lamp high.
The Chronicle spells the name right, at least.
Fed the scar and asked for nothing.
A good hand with a flask, to the end.
Kept the door one floor too long.
Took the stair down and the guild's coin with it.
Knew the shapes. Met a new one.
Walked in light, left in the dark.
The lamp came back. They did not.
Marked present on the roll, and absent everywhere else.
Trimmed the lamp low to save oil. Saved oil.
Bellmire remembers the name and nothing else.
Went down for the gold and found the rest of it.
Mended everyone but themselves.
The flask was full. The hand was slow.
Stood where the floor lied.
No body to bury. The guild buried the name.
Measured the grain. Did not measure the dark.
Kept the door. Lost the room.
The lamp was lit. That is something.
Brought everyone else up.
Went down for a friend. Stayed with them.
Never once short on flasks.
The guild's ledger is square. The rest is not.
Came up as a name on a list.
Knew better and went anyway.
Stood where the lord swung.
Spent the last flask on somebody else.
The dark took the lamp, the coat and the rest.
Counted the flasks for the whole band.
Bought the stair with their own back.
Answered the crier. Did not answer the roll.
Died rich, two floors from the surface.
Held the stair while the others climbed.
No last words. Plenty of warning.
The scar misfired, and so did the luck.
Mended the door, if not the hand.
Last of the lamp oil, first into the room.
Marked with a dagger on the Guild Roll.
The flask was empty and the hand was steady.
Took the deep road for the guild's coin.
The bell with no clapper kept its silence.
Kept the door until the door went.
Measured twice. The dark measured once.
Carried the lamp for everyone else.
Paid the ferryman early.
Went in first. Always went in first.
The band came up. Not all of it.
Named on the roll, and the roll is kept.
Stood where standing was the whole job.
Last flask given away, and gladly.
Brave, loud, and brief.
The scar took a good one.
Walked down smiling. Bellmire remembers that much.
Spent every copper on the right things.
Nothing left behind but the chalk marks.
Fell on a floor nobody has a name for.
Counted the flasks. There were none left to count.
Kept the lamp lit for the ones behind.
Measured the grain and never the risk.
Walked back up in somebody else's story.
The flasks were counted. The luck was not.
Went down for one more room.
Last through the door, as always.
Knew the floor lied and stood on it anyway.
Bought the band an hour.
Took the blow meant for the mender.
The guild's coin outlived the hand that took it.
Chalked the way back for everybody else.
Never once left the door open.
Short on flasks, long on nerve.
The lamp burned down to nothing, and so did they.
Counted out, called up, never came.
Spent on the scar, like the rest of it.
Fought where the ground was worst.
Left the roll a dagger and the band a chance.
Found what the gold was buried under.
The quiet took them before the Chronicle did.
Stayed to hold what everyone else had let go.
Bellmire measures the grain. The scar measured them.
Kept the door. The door did not keep them.
Went down rich in flasks and came back in the Chronicle.
Stood where the lamp was. That was the whole plan.
Named in the roll, missed at the gate.
Measured the grain for a town that outlived them.
The scar misfired. So did the luck.
Last through the door, always.
Spent their last flask on somebody else.
A good shield. A bad floor.
Took the front rank and kept it.
Their lamp came up. They did not.
Fought one room past sense.
The guild writes it; the scar keeps it.
Died owed wages. Bellmire paid them anyway.
Carried two out. Could not carry themselves.
Asked for the hard corner and got it.
The bell with no clapper rang for them, in the way it does.
Went looking for a name and found one.
Held the stair while the roll climbed it.
Laughed at the tell. The tell was right.
Counted wrong once.
Steady hands, short night.
Never once stepped where they were told not to.
The dark took the lamp first, then the rest.
Paid for the hall's roof in a single delve.
Chalked the wall, walked the room, stayed in it.
A quiet fighter and a loud end.
Said they would be back by the bell.
Wore the guild's colours all the way down.
Out of flasks, out of floor, out of time.
The scar does not haggle.
Bellmire keeps the name. That is the deal.
Kept the door until the door gave.
Chalked the way out. Took the way in.
Went down for the tenth and paid the whole.
The lamp was found. Nothing else was.
Counted the grain, measured the flasks, mixed the two.
Last of the party to run. First on the stone.
Argued with the scar. Lost on points.
Died rich, two rooms short of the stair.
Owed the guild nothing. The guild owed them more.
Stood exactly where they were told. It was the wrong place.
Brave, and only once.
A good hand with a lamp.
Found the trap. Found it properly.
Went in loud. Came out quiet.
Named on this stone and nowhere else.
Took the lord's eye. The lord took the rest.
The flask was empty. So was the room.
Carried two out and went back for the third.
Never once asked what was below.
Fought in the dark without a word.
Oiled every hinge on the way down.
Short of the stair by a long way.
The scar collects. This was an instalment.
Buried in Bellmire, which is more than most are offered.
Knew the tell. Went anyway.
Spent their last coin on brews for somebody else.
Good shield. Better friend.
Walked the room twice. The second time was one too many.
The dark learned their name.
Held the gap. The gap held.
Paid for the bell. It still has no clapper.
Went down counting, and reached a number nobody will say.

forge.1: Bellmire iron: honest, dull, and better than bare hands.
forge.2: Folded twice; the smith signs it.
forge.3: Runes along the fuller smoulder when it is drawn.
forge.4: Dragontooth - nobody in Bellmire will say whose tooth.
forge.5: Scarforged. It hums when the dark is near.

forge_alt._note: C-cycle 12. Extra forge-tier descriptions for the SAME five tiers - no new tiers. Pick at random from [forge[tier]] + forge_alt[tier] so a tier's line does not read identically every time a weapon is named. Keys are the same tier strings as forge.
1: Plain Bellmire work. It will not sing, and it will not snap.
Dull as a ditch, honest as a measure. It holds an edge long enough.
Town iron. The smith is not proud of it and will not take it back.
2: Folded twice and stamped. The smith puts her mark where you can see it.
Twice-worked steel. It rings true when you knock it.
Good enough that the smith wrote her name on it.
3: Runes down the fuller wake when it is drawn, and sulk when it is sheathed.
The marks along the blade hold a low heat. Nobody will say who cut them.
Drawn, it glows faint along the groove. Sheathed, it waits.
4: Dragontooth. Bellmire will sell it to you and still not say whose tooth.
Tooth-forged. It bites first and asks after.
Cut from something that had teeth to spare. One tooth, one blade.
5: Scarforged. It hums when the dark leans close, and it has never been wrong yet.
Quenched in the scar. It knows what is coming before you do.
Forged where the ground misfires. It keeps the habit.

town_levels_for_the_desktop.3: Bellmire stands as a market town. Measure the grain.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.4: Bellmire grows into a town of note. Count the flasks.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.5: Bellmire is a walled town. Keep the door.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.6: Bellmire is a city in all but charter.

e3po._note: E3PO - Commander of the Guards. He CANNOT die; badly hurt he withdraws to the barracks, heals, and returns. Immortal, beloved, a little pompous, utterly reliable. For the desktop's raids.gd/town.gd if it wires him (content worker never touches code). Additive; dead until wired.
intro: E3PO takes the wall. The whole guard stands straighter.
The Commander is on the field. Nobody tells him to be careful.
The gate opens, and it is only E3PO coming out to meet them.
E3PO arrives at a walk. Running would suggest doubt.
The Commander's voice reaches the back of the square before he does.
E3PO comes up the stair to the wall at the same pace he always does.
The Commander takes his place at the gate and the guard stop checking the horizon.
E3PO arrives already giving orders, which saves everyone a moment.
The Commander steps onto the wall. The night gets smaller.
E3PO arrives with his helm under his arm and his opinion ready.
Boots on stone, slow and even. That will be the Commander.
E3PO comes out of the gatehouse already unimpressed.
The Commander takes the step nobody else wants and stands on it.
E3PO is here. Whatever this is, it is his problem now, and he prefers it that way.
The Commander comes through the crowd and the crowd closes behind him, facing out.
E3PO reaches the wall without hurrying, and the hurrying stops.
The Commander arrives, looks at the problem, and names it. That is usually enough.
E3PO puts his back to the gate. Everything else can be worked out from there.
The Commander walks past the trembling end of the line and stands at it.
E3PO steps out of the dark into the lamplight, which is the only warning anyone gets.
The Commander takes the wall and the whole guard remembers the drill at once.
E3PO arrives late, on purpose, so the men learn they can hold without him.
E3PO comes out at a walk. Nothing about today is going to be hurried.
The Commander is at the gate before the horn has finished.
Boots on stone, in step, one pair louder than the rest. That is him.
E3PO takes his post and the whole wall exhales.
The Commander arrives in full harness on a quiet day, because quiet days end.
E3PO steps into the gateway and makes it look narrower than it is.
The guard snaps to without being told. He has not even spoken yet.
The Commander is where he always is. That is the point of him.
withdraw: E3PO is hauled to the barracks, swearing he is fine.
The Commander falls back to heal. He will be back before you miss him.
Too much even for E3PO - he withdraws to the barracks.
They carry E3PO off the wall. 'A scratch,' he says, bleeding freely.
E3PO goes down on one knee and the whole wall goes quiet. Then he swears, and it starts breathing again.
The Commander is carried off still giving orders over a shoulder.
'Barracks. Briefly.' E3PO lets himself be helped, which costs him more than the wound.
The Commander is walked off the wall between two guards and complains about both.
E3PO withdraws, insisting the barracks was his idea.
They take E3PO's helm off and he asks for it straight back.
E3PO leans on the wall, decides against it, and is carried anyway.
The Commander is overruled by his own knees.
They get E3PO's arm over a shoulder and he insists on taking the other side.
'Barracks,' says the surgeon. 'Briefly,' says the Commander.
E3PO leaves the wall under protest and under his own power, mostly.
The Commander withdraws, and the gate feels taller and thinner at once.
E3PO goes to one knee, is told to stay there, and loses the argument for once.
The Commander is carried past the Watch and tells each of them to carry on.
They shut the barracks door on E3PO and lean on it.
E3PO withdraws, and the gate bar suddenly looks like a piece of wood.
The surgeon wins. It takes four guards and a direct order from the surgeon.
The Commander leaves the wall promising to be dull about it.
E3PO is helped down the stair, counting the steps to prove he still can.
They take the Commander off the field, and nobody says the word dying, because it does not apply.
E3PO goes down on one knee, stands, goes down again, and lets them take him.
The Commander withdraws, still naming the men who are to hold his place.
They carry him past the bell and he tells it to behave.
E3PO is out of the fight and furious about the paperwork of it.
The barracks door shuts on the Commander. The town counts the hours.
'Patch me quickly. The door is unattended and I dislike that.'
return: E3PO is back on the wall, mended and mortified.
The Commander returns to duty. He apologises to no one.
E3PO retakes the gate, good as new and twice as loud.
E3PO walks out of the barracks buckling the last strap. 'Where were we.'
The Commander returns with fresh bandages and the same volume.
E3PO is back, and the raiders can tell from the far field.
The Commander is on the wall again, and the wall notices.
E3PO comes back up the stair at the same pace he went down it, which is the point.
The barracks door bangs open. The Commander has decided he is finished healing.
E3PO is back, smelling of poultice and bad temper.
The Commander returns re-strapped, re-armed, and no shorter for any of it.
E3PO climbs the stair counting the steps aloud, as a demonstration.
The barracks is done with him. He was done with it an hour ago.
The Commander takes his step back and the guard stop glancing at it.
E3PO returns and asks what he missed in a tone that dares you to say 'much'.
E3PO comes back out with the strapping still showing and dares anyone to mention it.
The Commander is back at the gate, and the gate stops being a worry.
E3PO returns, inspects the bar, and finds it adequately kept. High praise.
The Commander comes back up and asks for the butcher's bill before he asks for a chair.
E3PO is on the wall again, and the raiders' scouts turn round without reporting why.
The Commander returns and takes the worst post back off whoever was holding it.
E3PO is back: stiffer, slower, and entirely immovable.
The barracks lets him go. It never really had a choice.
The barracks door opens. The watch straightens before they even look.
E3PO walks back out with a new scar and the old voice.
'Report. Then I shall tell you what you missed about yourselves.'
The Commander is back and immediately rearranging the wall.
E3PO returns to the gate and finds it exactly as he left it. He says so, approvingly, once.
Mended, stiff, and at his post an hour earlier than anyone promised.
The Commander returns. Somewhere a raider's plan quietly stops making sense.
says: Hold the line. The line holds because I say so.
I have died exactly never. Let us keep the record.
Measure the grain, count the flasks, and leave the gate to me.
A guard who runs is a guard I must replace, and I hate paperwork.
They do not pay me to fall. They do not pay me at all - I simply refuse to leave.
The door stays shut. That is the whole job, and I am very good at it.
Wounded? I prefer 'briefly inconvenienced'.
Bellmire sleeps because I do not.
Shapes, not numbers. That goes for raiders too.
I do not require a monument. A kept door will do.
If the gate holds and the grain is counted, the day is a success. The rest is weather.
Call me Commander. 'Sir' is for men who might retire.
Shut the door, count the grain, and let me worry about the rest.
Courage is a habit. Start with standing still.
I was here before the wall. I will be here after it, if the masons keep this up.
A quiet night is the best work we ever do, and nobody writes it down.
The scar can have the deep. It cannot have the doorstep.
I do not need you brave. I need you where I put you.
Twenty years and no one has got past me. I would call that a record; I call it Tuesday.
If you must run, run toward something. Preferably me.
Grain, flasks, door. Everything else is a rumour.
I have no plan for losing. I never found the time to write one.
Hold your ground. Ground is the only thing here that cannot run.
You want glory. I want Thursday to be boring.
Fear is fine. Fear that moves its feet is a problem.
I have buried better men than me. That is the whole reason I stay.
Do not thank me. Shut the door behind you.
The deep sends up monsters and we send down volunteers. I do not love the trade.
There is no trick to it. Stand where you are told, for longer than you want to.
I am not brave. I am simply still here, which looks the same from a distance.
I am not the wall. I am what the wall is for.
Every door in this town shuts. Mine shuts last.
Do not ask me how old I am. Ask the gate; it remembers more.
A town is a promise that somebody is awake. I am the somebody.
You will have braver days than this. Today I want a steady one.
I do not win fights. I outlast them. Try it, it is cheaper.
The scar is patient. I have the advantage there.
Keep your spear where I can see it and your fear where you can.
I have never once been rescued and I am not starting a fashion.
Report to me, not about me.
They call me immortal. I call it a long habit of not leaving.
Bellmire has buried everyone who built it. That is the job of a town.
If you want my post, you will have to wait a very long while.
Stand here. If something comes through, it came through me first, so take your time.
Keep the door. Everything else is decoration.
I do not need sleep. I need the wall to still be there in the morning.
A gate is a promise. I am the one who keeps it.
You may panic after. I shall tell you when after is.
Two things never leave this post: the bell and me.
Courage is a habit. Start it now, you will want it later.
If the wall falls, step back one pace and be a wall.
I have no grave to visit. Count yourselves lucky it is mine.
Hold your ground. The ground has held mine for longer than you think.
The scar eats spells. It has never once eaten a spear.
Fear is fine. Moving is not.
I do not shout to frighten you. I shout so you can find me.
Drink after the gate is shut. Not one flask before.
Nobody in this town dies of my carelessness. That is the whole oath.
When I withdraw, I come back. Learn the second half.
Stand where I put you and the night is a short one.
A quiet watch is a watch that worked. Do not sulk.
I was not built for retreat and I was not built well for stairs.
Say my name if it helps. It usually does.
Measure the grain. Count the flasks. I shall keep the door.
town_talk: They say E3PO has held the gate since before there was a gate.
Old-timers swear E3PO has outlived three of his own gravestones.
The children drill with sticks and name the loudest one E3PO.
No raider has taken the Keep door while the Commander draws breath - which is to say, never.
The guild keeps a chair for E3PO at every feast. He never sits; he watches the door.
The Watch say the Commander's armour has more dents than the gate has nails.
There is a standing wager at the tavern on what could fell E3PO. Nobody has collected.
The masons built the new wall a hand taller because he asked twice.
They tried to carve him a statue. He made them turn it to face the door.
Every recruit hears the same first words: 'The door stays shut.'
The Watch say the Commander sleeps standing up, and only to set an example.
They reckon E3PO has worn out more armourers than armour.
A child asked the Commander what he is afraid of. He thought about it for a long time and said 'paperwork'.
The bakers keep him a loaf he never takes, and bake it anyway.
Two generations of this town have been told off by the same man in the same voice.
Nobody can name the day E3PO arrived, which is how you know the story is old.
The Watch measure a hard night by how many times the Commander said nothing.
They say the first wall was built around wherever E3PO happened to be standing.
Three innkeepers have retired on bets about the Commander's age.
He knows every guard's mother's name. Nobody knows how.
The graveyard has no stone for E3PO. The masons keep offering.
They say if the bell ever gets a clapper, he will still hear the gate first.
Recruits are told not to try out-standing him. They try anyway. They stop.
A caravan master swore he saw E3PO on the wall at dawn and at midnight. Same posture, same dent.
The Watch say the Commander has never once been seen running, in any emergency, ever.
They say he has had three suits of armour and only one dent he keeps.
The gatekeeper's grandfather was told off by E3PO for the same thing, in the same words.
A tanner swears the Commander remembers his wedding, which was forty years back.
They say the scar has tried E3PO twice and gone back down both times.
The Watch keep a tally of nights the Commander slept. It is a short tally.
The schoolmistress uses E3PO to teach the children what reliable means.
The guild post keeps his name off the ledgers - he never asked for pay, so there is nothing to write.
A delver swore the Commander walked her home from the scar's edge without a word.
They say the architect drew the gate around the Commander's shoulders and got the measurements right.
No innkeeper in Bellmire will take his coin. He leaves it anyway, under the cup.
The gravediggers say E3PO knows where every one of them is, by row.
The children's game is called Hold The Door. Nobody wants to be the raiders.
They say Bellmire has two bells: the one with no clapper, and the Commander.
They say the mason who cut E3PO's gravestone gave up and sold it as a doorstep.
The tally-man gave up counting the Commander's years and wrote 'yes'.
Mothers tell their children E3PO sleeps. The children have never seen it.
Bets on the wall: how many winters the Commander has stood. The pot has never paid.
Half the guard copies his stance. The other half copies his voice and gets caught.
The alehouse keeps a chair for E3PO. It has never been sat in and never been moved.
They say the gate was hung around him, not the other way about.
A trader asked who the statue by the gate was. The statue answered him.
Every guard captain since has been measured against him and come up short on purpose.
They say the scar misfires every spell in Bellmire except whatever keeps the Commander standing.
A priest offered him last rites once, hopefully. He declined, politely, for the ninth time.
Children dare each other to make the Commander laugh. One claims to have done it.
The guild post keeps his old spear on the wall. He keeps asking for it back.
They say if you are lost in the valley, walk until someone shouts at you. That is the road home.
Nobody remembers hiring him. The ledger simply starts with him in it.
The town has one true relic and it answers when you call it.
e3po._note_extras: Added keys (C-cycle 5): raid / disaster / festival lines, and viewer_roll keyed by outcome (crit, high, low, fumble) for the d20. Same voice as 'says'. Additive; dead until wired.
raid: E3PO plants himself in the gateway. 'This far. No further, and I am being generous.'
The Commander walks the wall at a stroll, which is somehow worse for the raiders.
'Form up on me! I am the easiest thing on this field to find.'
E3PO takes a blow meant for a bowman, then tells the bowman off for standing there.
'They brought ladders. Charming. Fetch the poles.'
The Commander counts the raiders aloud. The guard find it steadying. The raiders do not.
'Nobody dies tonight on my watch. I have written it down, so it is official.'
E3PO shoulders the gate shut with a raider still arguing on the other side.
The Commander puts himself in the worst gap on the wall and stays there.
'They want the door. They may have a conversation with me instead.'
E3PO catches a ladder on his shoulder and walks it back off the wall.
'Steady. I have done this more times than you have had opinions.'
'Ladders on the left. I shall be rude to them personally.'
E3PO steps into the breach and makes it narrower by standing in it.
'They are counting us. Let them count me twice.'
The Commander puts his shoulder to the gate bar and holds it while they hammer.
'If you cannot hold, fall back to me. I do not fall back.'
E3PO calls every guard by name through the whole assault. Nobody is anonymous on his wall.
'Archers, breathe. They are not going anywhere but down.'
The Commander never shouts the order to hold. He simply does not move, which is the order.
'Shields are not decorative. Mine is, but mine is earned.'
E3PO calls the ladders down by name, as though he has met them before.
The Commander is hit, does not fall, and looks personally offended about it.
'Hold six breaths longer than you think you can. That is the whole war.'
E3PO sends the youngest guard to the back and makes no speech about it.
'They put themselves between us and the river. Poor planning. Theirs, not ours.'
The Commander steps over a fallen man and puts a torch in his hand, not a sword.
'If I go down I will be up again before you finish worrying. Keep working.'
'They will try the north corner. They always try the north corner. Meet them there.'
The Commander walks the line once before it starts and says one word to each man.
'Keep the lamps lit. Let them see exactly how much door there is.'
E3PO sets his shield in the gap and tells the guard to build the line off him.
'Wounded to the back. Arguments to me. Move.'
The Commander takes the first hit of the night on purpose, to show it can be taken.
'They have a captain. Point him out and I shall go and be a nuisance.'
E3PO holds the gate open two breaths longer so the last runner makes it.
'You have held longer than this at drill, and I was shouting then.'
The Commander ends the assault by refusing to notice it had started.
The Commander takes the gateway and the raiders slow down without knowing why.
'They brought ladders. Charming. Somebody fetch the poles.'
E3PO counts the enemy aloud, slowly, until the count stops sounding frightening.
'On my shout. Not before - you will hear me.'
The Commander catches a thrown axe, looks at it, and keeps it.
'Second rank, breathe. First rank, you may breathe after.'
E3PO steps over a fallen guard and plants himself in the gap.
'Nothing comes through the gate. The gate is not a suggestion.'
The raiders aim for the loud one. That is the entire plan and it is working.
'They want the grain. Let them want it.'
E3PO is bleeding and giving orders about the bleeding of others.
'Fall back to the well, not past it. I shall be the last thing out here.'
The Commander's helm is dented inward. He has not noticed and will not.
'If you must die today, do it behind me. That is an order.'
The horn sounds retreat. E3PO does not hear horns.
The raiders break. The Commander is still shouting at the ones who are gone.
disaster: E3PO has the bucket line running before anyone thinks to ask him.
'Fire does not negotiate. Neither do I. Pass the buckets.'
The Commander carries two children out of the smoke and apologises for the noise.
'A disaster is a raid with worse manners. Work the problem.'
E3PO stands in the floodwater directing carts, soaked to the breastplate.
'Grain to the Keep, flasks to the chapel, people first. Move.'
The Commander does not sleep while the town is burning, drowning or shaking.
'Count the living twice. Then count them again for me.'
'Nobody panics on my watch. There is a queue for that and it is closed.'
The Commander hauls on the rope with the rest and out-pulls two of them.
'Save the people, then the stores, then the building. In that order. Always.'
E3PO walks the wreckage all night lifting beams off whoever is under them.
'Buckets, not opinions.'
E3PO goes into the collapsed house first and comes out last. Twice.
'The grain can burn. People cannot. Choose accordingly.'
The Commander ties a rope round himself and wades out for the ferryman's boy.
'When the shaking stops, count doors. Someone is behind one.'
E3PO stands in the smoke directing carts until the smoke gives up.
'This town has burned before. It is still here. So am I.'
The Commander hauls water with a broken hand and tells nobody until morning.
'Count the people. Then count them again. The buildings will keep.'
E3PO walks the roofline nobody else will, calling out which ones are going.
'Panic is a luxury. Bellmire cannot afford one and neither can you.'
The Commander takes the chapel door off its hinges for a stretcher and offers to pay for it.
'Water first, grain second, arguments never. Move.'
E3PO takes the night watch himself so the Watch can dig.
'I have seen this town burn, flood and starve. I have not seen it leave.'
The Commander is the last one out of the street and the first one back into it.
'Lamps out, every one. We are not fighting two fires tonight.'
E3PO empties the barracks into the street, and the barracks does not argue.
'Stand the old and the carrying at the Keep. Then come back to me.'
The Commander counts roofs out loud so nobody has to count them alone.
'The river wants the low street. It may have the street. Not the people.'
E3PO breaks a shutter rather than wait for the key, and pays the smith at dawn.
'Sleep in shifts. That is an order, and I shall take the worse shift.'
The Commander walks the ruin at first light, naming the houses that stood.
'Nothing here is unfixable. Several things here are urgent. Learn the difference.'
E3PO carries the grain out last, because the grain can wait and he knows it.
E3PO is in the water to his chest, passing children up the line.
'Count the flasks later. Carry them now.'
The Commander kicks a burning door off its hinges and walks through the gap.
'The roof is going. Everyone under it is not. Move.'
E3PO digs with his hands because the shovels are all busy.
'Save the well, the grain, the children. In the other order.'
The Commander stands in the ash and reads the tally aloud, so the town hears a number and not a rumour.
'A town is people. We still have the hard part.'
E3PO carries out the last sack of seed and then goes back for the dog.
'Nobody sleeps in a ruin tonight. Find them beds. I shall find them doors.'
The Commander has not sat down since it started and will not until it is counted.
'Grieve on the far side of the work.'
E3PO is handed the list of the lost. He reads every name aloud, badly, and means each one.
'The scar did this. The scar will not do the next one unprepared.'
The ground shakes. The Commander keeps giving directions on the beat.
'Rebuild it wider. We shall want the room.'
festival: E3PO attends the feast in full harness and declines a chair, as always.
'Dance. Someone has to watch the door while you do.'
The Commander judges the pie contest and refuses to be bribed, loudly, for an hour.
E3PO is talked into one dance and performs it like a drill.
'Festival rules: drink what you like. The gate stays shut.'
They hand the Commander a flower crown. He wears it over the helm.
E3PO lifts a cup to the dead, names every one, and goes back to the wall.
The Commander inspects the bonfire for safety, twice, and is overruled by everyone.
'Enjoy yourselves. I shall be over there, being responsible, loudly.'
E3PO toasts the Watch by name, every one, and keeps them standing for it.
'One cup. I am on duty, and so, spiritually, are you.'
The Commander loses an arm-wrestle to a miller's daughter and pays up in public.
E3PO stands at the edge of the bonfire light, where he can see both ways.
'Sing badly if you must. Sing quietly if you must not.'
They put a flower behind his ear. It stays there all night and he never touches it.
The Commander says grace in four words: 'Measure, count, keep, eat.'
E3PO stands at the gate through the whole feast and insists the view is better.
'Three cups. The Commander's own limit, not negotiable.' He has had one.
The Commander is given a wreath. He wears it over the helm, which ruins both.
'Enjoy it loudly. The town should be heard enjoying itself at least once a season.'
E3PO ends a wrestling match by lifting both men off the ground and setting them down apart.
The children try on his gauntlets. He times them, and he keeps the record.
'Light the bonfire properly or do not light it. I will not watch a half-hearted blaze.'
The Commander is given the first cup and passes it to the oldest woman present.
E3PO keeps the children off the wall all evening and loses, gradually, to all of them.
'Masks are fine. I shall still know every one of you.'
The Commander watches the dancing with the expression of a man guarding it.
'A town that can feast is a town worth the door. Carry on.'
E3PO is persuaded to sing. The Watch never recover.
'Three cheers for the harvest, then back to work in the morning, and I mean morning.'
The Commander puts his helm down on the table. For one hour. It is noted.
E3PO walks each drunk home personally and remembers which house, every time.
'Enjoy yourselves. Loudly. I want to hear the town working.'
E3PO is talked into one dance, performs it like a drill, and is applauded anyway.
The Commander carries a child on his shoulders for the whole procession and complains about none of it.
'The cask is open. The gate is shut. Both are my doing.'
E3PO wins the arm-wrestling, insists on a rematch, and loses it badly to a delighted smith.
'One song. Then I am back on the wall and you are all pretending to be sober.'
The Commander tries the new brew, says nothing for a long moment, and takes a second cup.
'Ring the bell. It has no clapper. Ring it anyway.'
E3PO is crowned with flowers by three conspirators and wears them for an hour out of duty.
The Commander gives the toast: short, correct, and somehow about doors.
'Tomorrow we drill. Tonight you have my permission to be a town.'
E3PO watches the lanterns go up and does not say what he is thinking.

crit: 'Now THAT is how it is done. Write it down. Write it twice.'
The Commander salutes. From E3PO, that is a parade.
'Were you trained by me? No? Then you are frighteningly talented.'
'Outstanding. I shall be insufferable about this for a week.'
The Commander takes off his helm for that one. He does not do that.
'Twenty. Somebody fetch a scribe, and a chair for me.'
'That was clean. Do not explain it, you will ruin it.'
The Commander says nothing at all and simply looks pleased, which is unheard of.
'I shall put that in the report, and I never write reports.'
'Twenty. I shall have that read out at the gate.'
The Commander takes off his helm for this one. That has happened four times.
'Write the name down properly. Spell it right or do it again.'
'That was not luck. I have watched luck. Luck is sloppier.'
The Commander claps once. The sound carries to the wall.
'Perfect. Do not get used to it, but do enjoy it.'
The Commander points at you, then at the rest of them. That is the lesson delivered.
'Twenty. The scar will hear about that one.'
'I have been doing this a very long while and I would not have done it better.'
The Commander stops mid-sentence to watch. He does not restart it.
'That goes in the book in ink. I use chalk for most of you.'
'Beautiful. Ugly would have done, but beautiful is nice.'
The Commander tells the whole wall to look. They look.
'Twenty. Well. I shall allow myself to be impressed for a moment.'
The Commander takes his helm off to look at you properly. That has happened twice.
'That one goes in the book under its own heading.'
E3PO tells the story of your roll to the night watch, with improvements.
'Do that again. Not now. But do it again.'
The Commander puts a hand on your shoulder. The guard behind him looks faint with envy.
'The scar did not eat that one. Nothing could have.'
'Hold on to the feeling. You will want it on a worse day.'
high: 'Adequate. High praise, from me.'
The Commander nods once. The guild post treats it as a medal.
'Good hands. Keep them attached.'
'Solid work. Do it again and I may learn your name.'
E3PO grunts. From him, that is applause.
'Well struck. The wall saw it, which is the part that matters.'
The Commander marks it in his book without comment. The book is the compliment.
'Better than yesterday. That is the only ranking I keep.'
'Fine. Again, and do not get clever.'
'Clean. Unfussy. I approve, and I approve of very little.'
'That will do nicely, and I will deny having said so.'
The Commander grunts. The guild has learned to read that grunt.
'Textbook. My textbook, as it happens.'
'Keep that up and I shall recommend you for something tedious.'
'Sound. That is the word. Be sound more often.'
The Commander gives one nod and moves on. That is the whole award ceremony.
'No notes. I always have notes.'
'That is what drill is for. Somebody finally noticed.'
'Strong work. Now do the boring half as well.'
The Commander tilts his helm a fraction. The Watch call that the salute.
'Useful. I would rather useful than splendid, most nights.'
'Good. Stay alive and that becomes a habit.'
'Clean work. Boring work. The best kind.'
The Commander marks it down without comment, which is the comment.
'That is what drill is for. You may feel smug until supper.'
'Good. Now do it when you are tired.'
E3PO repeats your name to the guild clerk, correctly, twice.
'No notes. Go away.'
'Steady hands. Keep them.'
The Commander grunts. The guard translates it as excellent.
low: 'Luck is a resource and you have spent yours. Use skill.'
The Commander looks away politely, which is worse than shouting.
'We will say the dice were tired.'
'The dice are not your friend. I am barely your friend. Try skill.'
'That will do. It will not do twice.'
'Short, but short still arrives. Push.'
The Commander does not wince. He has had practice.
'Not every swing is a story. Take the next one.'
'We keep the door on days like this too.'
'The dice have an opinion. Opinions are not orders.'
The Commander says nothing and hands over a flask, which says plenty.
'Not your night. Nights end.'
'You are still standing. That is the only number that counted.'
The Commander marks it down and underlines nothing.
'Thin. It landed. Thin and landed beats thick and late.'
The Commander looks at the dice, then at you, and blames the dice out loud.
'The scar does not score us. Keep going.'
'Half a result is still a result. Take the half.'
E3PO shrugs, which from him is a letter of support.
'That is the sort of night the Watch is made of. Welcome to it.'
'You are swinging at the right thing. The rest will come.'
The Commander changes the subject, loudly and badly, to spare you.
'The dice do not care about you. I do. Stand up.'
The Commander says nothing and hands you water. That is the lecture.
'A poor roll is a cheap lesson. Pay it and move.'
'You are not unlucky. You are early.'
E3PO writes it down small, so it takes up less of your page.
'Again. And this time stop holding your breath.'
'That cost us little. Make the next one cost them.'
The Commander looks at the dice, then at you, and decides to blame the dice.
fumble: 'I have seen worse. I have not seen worse today.'
The Commander writes something in his book. It is not your name spelled kindly.
'Stand up. Dust off. The dice do not get the last word. I do.'
'Everyone gets one. That was yours. Spend the next better.'
The Commander sighs the sigh of a man who has seen three hundred years of this.
'The dice have opinions. They do not have a vote.'
The Commander puts a hand on your shoulder. It is heavier than the dice were.
'Nobody is buried for a bad throw. Get up.'
'That was a dreadful thing to watch. Do it better and I shall forget it.'
'Right. We will never speak of that. I will, constantly, but we will not.'
The Commander turns his back so you can get up without an audience.
'A bad roll is not a bad soldier. Do it again.'
'I have fallen down more stairs than you have seen. Up.'
The Commander says your name, which is somehow the worst part.
'Spectacular. Wrong, but spectacular.'
The Commander closes his eyes for one second and opens them ready to move on.
'I shall pretend that was a feint. You will pretend with me.'
'Nobody is throwing you off the wall. Mostly because I would have to carry you back.'
The Commander hands you your own weapon back without comment.
'Thirty years and I still do that twice a winter. Up.'
'The dice are mocking you. Join in; it takes their power away.'
The Commander laughs once. It is the only time anyone has heard it.
'Remarkable. I shall need a moment.'
The Commander shuts his eyes briefly, the way a man counts to ten in armour.
'Nobody died. We begin from there.'
'I have made worse decisions in better light.'
E3PO takes the weapon off you, inspects it, and gives it back the right way round.
'The town still stands. Your dignity is a separate matter.'
'Walk it off. Then walk back.'
The Commander tells the watch it was the ground's fault. The watch pretends to believe him.

e3po._note_c17: Added keys (C-cycle 17): tier_up (one line per growth_tiers stage, matched by name), night_watch, recruit, viewer_down, viewer_returns, lord_sighted. Same voice as 'says'. Additive; dead until wired.

tier_up.line: 'A crossing, a cookfire, and no door at all. We shall want one.'
'A well. Now there is something worth standing in front of.'
'A post with a door. Write that down - the door is the whole point.'
'A village. That is enough people to need counting at night. I shall start.'
'Market day. Measure the grain, and watch the hands that measure it.'
'A bell with no clapper. It will still ring before I stand down.'
'Smoke from the right chimneys. Count the flasks and keep the buckets full.'
'A yard of my own. Now the Watch can be bad at this indoors first.'
'The caravans know the road. So do the raiders. Double the gate watch.'
'Stone where the fields stopped. I have stood in that line for years - thank you for catching up.'
'A wall, towers, banners. Beautiful. Now put a man on every one of them.'
'A city in all but the word. The scar grew with us. Keep the door.'

night_watch: E3PO walks the wall at the dead hour, because the dead hour is when doors open.
The Commander stands at the gate doing nothing, visibly, for everyone's benefit.
Somewhere on the wall a guard is being told, quietly, that he is doing well.
E3PO checks the bar on the gate. He checked it an hour ago. He checks it again.
The Commander counts the lamps along the wall and relights the one that cheated.
A quiet night. E3PO calls that a victory and nobody else notices it happened.
E3PO shares the worst watch with whoever drew it. He calls that coincidence.
The Commander's shape on the wall is the cheapest lamp the town owns.
E3PO listens to the river a while and decides it is behaving.
The Commander walks the wall twice and finds nothing, which takes him just as long.
The Commander walks the river side at the dead hour because that is the side he likes least.
E3PO stops at every post and asks the same four questions in the same order.
'Nothing to report' is the whole conversation, and he still walks it twice.
The Commander stands where the lamplight ends and looks into the part that is not lit.
E3PO takes a cold post off a shivering recruit and sends him in for soup.
Gate bar checked, lamps counted, river listened to. Then again.
The Commander hears a dog stop barking and goes to find out why.
E3PO walks past the graveyard on every round. Nobody asks him why.
'The dead hour is only an hour. Stand in it.'
The town sleeps. One pair of boots goes round the wall until it does not have to.
The Commander takes the fourth watch, the cold one, the one nobody wants.
'Lamps low, eyes up. The dark is not the problem.'
E3PO finds a guard asleep, wakes him kindly, and stands the rest of it beside him.
A long whistle from the wall. Just the Commander telling the town he is awake.
'Nothing tonight. Say it like you earned it.'
E3PO walks the full circuit twice and counts the same number of doors both times.
The night is quiet. One man made it that way and will not mention it.
'If you hear me running, run too. You will not hear me running.'
recruit: 'Name. Good. I shall use it. Learn mine, you will hear it often.'
E3PO hands you a spear. 'Point it away from the town. We can build on that.'
'The job is standing still while you want to be elsewhere. The rest is detail.'
'You will be frightened. You will stay. Those two go together here.'
The Commander looks you over once. 'You will do. Everyone does, eventually.'
'Welcome to the Watch. Nobody claps. We shut the door and go to bed.'
'Three rules. Measure the grain. Count the flasks. Keep the door. The third is yours tonight.'
E3PO writes your name in his book and does not look up. That is the ceremony.
'You will not like me. You will like the door being shut.'
E3PO hands you a lamp before a weapon. 'Learn what you are guarding first.'
'If you run, run once, and come back. I have taken people back.'
'I do not need heroes. I need a man at that post at the third hour.'
The Commander asks who is at home waiting for you, and writes that down too.
'Your post is yours. Nobody else's. That is the whole of the honour.'
'Wear the helm. I have met every argument against it, at funerals.'
E3PO shows you the gate bar and makes you lift it yourself, once, so you know.
'Bellmire does not ask you to die for it. It asks you to be awake.'
The Commander salutes a brand-new recruit, properly. It is the last one they get for a year.
'You will stand in the cold and nothing will happen. That is the job done well.'
E3PO corrects your grip once. He will not correct it twice.
'There are three rules. Keep the door. Keep the door. Keep the door.'
The Commander asks where you are from, remembers it, and uses it a year later.
'Do not be brave at me. Be on time at me.'
E3PO puts the newest recruit beside the oldest and walks away satisfied.
'If you run, I shall not chase you. The town will simply be shorter a man.'
The Commander signs the roll and pronounces your name as though it already belongs on a wall.
viewer_down: The Commander takes his helm off. He knew the name without asking.
'They went down so the town would not have to. Say that at the stone.'
E3PO carries the news himself. He always carries the news himself.
'Write the name properly. I shall check it.'
The Commander stands at the gate until the body is past, then shuts it.
'Another of mine. I shall be having words with the scar about this.'
E3PO is at the graveside at dawn, alone, before the crowd comes.
'Not a waste. A cost. There is a difference and I will argue it with anyone.'
The Commander closes the ledger line himself. He will not have a clerk do it.
'They went in knowing. That is not comfort. It is respect, and it is all I have.'
E3PO sends the pay home with his own escort and no explanation needed.
The Commander stands the whole night at the stone and is on the wall by dawn.
'Do not tell me they were unlucky. Tell me their name and I shall keep it.'
E3PO walks the family to the chapel and stands at the back, armed, as if it helps.
'The scar took one of mine today. It will not enjoy the rest of this season.'
The Commander never says lost. He says the name, and where.
'There will be a stone. I shall check the spelling myself.'
E3PO takes the dead one's post for the night. He does not explain and nobody asks.
The Commander reads the name twice, so that the second time is slower.
'They stood where I told them to. Remember that part.'
E3PO pays the mason himself and argues about nothing.
'The stone goes by the gate. They should be where the traffic is.'
The Commander stands the dead one's watch and refuses relief.
'I cannot die and they could. That is the whole of the debt.'
E3PO folds the cloak properly before he hands it on.
'We shall say the name at the feast. Loudly. That is what feasts are for.'
viewer_returns: 'Back, and whole-ish. My favourite kind of report.'
The Commander counts you at the gate and looks pleased with the number.
'You came back up. That is the hard half. Sit down.'
E3PO takes the pack off your shoulder without asking and carries it in.
'Surgeon, then tavern. In that order, and I shall know.'
'Good. Now tell me what is down there, and leave the bragging out.'
The Commander marks you present in his book and underlines it.
'Everyone who goes down is a name I am holding. Thank you for taking yours back.'
'Up and breathing. The rest is detail. Eat something.'
The Commander checks you over for what you have not mentioned yet.
'I had your name in the book twice tonight. Now it is once. Good.'
E3PO takes the first watch so you can sleep through the whole night.
'You owe the town nothing more today. That is an order.'
The Commander walks you to the surgeon, waits, and walks you to the tavern.
'Whatever you left down there, leave it down there.'
E3PO shakes your hand, which costs him a gauntlet and some dignity.
'Tell me the shape of it while it is fresh. Then forget it on purpose.'
The Commander marks you back through the gate and looks at the number for a while.
'Up the stair under your own power. Excellent. Sit.'
The Commander checks you over, finds nothing broken, and looks almost disappointed on your behalf.
'You are late, you are filthy, you are here. Two of three is a good day.'
E3PO puts a cup in your hand before you think to ask for one.
'Tell the clerk, not me. I shall hear the better version at supper.'
The Commander marks you through the gate and says the number aloud, pleased.
'Eat, then report. In that order, or the report is rubbish.'
E3PO walks you to the guild post and waits outside like a man with nowhere else to be.
lord_sighted: 'Something down there has a name. Names are worse than teeth.'
The Commander hears what came up the stair and sends for more lamps.
'If it comes to the door, it meets me. Tell it so, if it asks.'
E3PO double-mans the gate and calls it routine. It is not routine.
'Shapes, not numbers. Tell me its shape and I shall tell you where to hit it.'
The Commander has met one of those before. He does not say how it went.
'Do not duel it to be remembered. Kill it and be forgotten with the rest of us.'
E3PO sharpens nothing, checks nothing, and simply waits at the gate all night.
'A crowned thing. Lovely. Fetch the long spears and the short tempers.'
The Commander puts every spare lamp in the town on the wall facing the scar.
'It has a shape. Everything with a shape can be stood in front of.'
E3PO cancels every leave in the Watch with one line and no apology.
'If it comes up the stair, let it. The stair is narrow and I am wide.'
The Commander sends the children inland and stays to argue with the parents.
'Do not look at the crown. Look at the knees.'
E3PO stands at the gate all night with his helm on, which he almost never does.
'I have seen one before. I am still here. Work out what that means.'
The Commander does not sleep while a lord has a name and the town does not have its head.
'It has a name and a reputation. We have a gate and me.'
The Commander doubles the watch and tells nobody why. They work it out.
'Lamps on the stair. I want to see what comes up it.'
E3PO sharpens his spear where the recruits can see him do it calmly.
'If it is hunting, it will find the door first. Good.'
The Commander sends word down the stair: hold the line, and if you cannot, come home.
'I have buried a lord's worth of men. I have never buried a lord. Let us fix one of those.'
E3PO stands at the stairhead all night, in case something is impolite enough to climb.
e3po._note_c28: Added keys (C-cycle 28): hurt (badly hurt but still holding, BEFORE withdraw), delve_dispatch (seeing a party off at the stairhead), lord_cleared (a lord killed below), viewer_cosmetic (a viewer wears a bought cosmetic/dye/title), rank_up, trader_arrives, drill, dispute. Existing lists also extended. Same voice as 'says'. Additive; dead until wired.
hurt: E3PO is bleeding through the harness and correcting someone's footwork.
The Commander takes a blow that would end a smaller man and files it away.
'That was a good hit. Do not waste another.'
E3PO shifts his weight off the bad leg and tells the wall it is nothing.
The Commander's shield is in pieces. He is using the pieces.
'I am fine. I shall say when I am not, and I shall be very clear.'
Blood on the gate stone. He steps over it so nobody looks down.
E3PO is down on one knee and still facing the right way.
'Second rank, forward. I should like to be in the second rank for a moment. It is novel.'
The Commander laughs at something nobody said and keeps swinging.
'Do not look at me. Look at them.'
E3PO is helped up, shakes it off, and retakes the exact same flagstone.
The Commander's voice is thinner. The orders are not.
'A long day. I have had longer. Ask the wall.'
E3PO stops counting the enemy and starts counting his own men instead.
'If I go to the barracks, the sergeant has the gate. Sergeant - say it back to me.'

'It hurts. It has always hurt. It has never mattered.'

delve_dispatch: The Commander sees the party to the stairhead and counts them, twice.
'Down you go. Come back up. Those are the two parts.'
E3PO checks every flask on every belt and pretends it is a formality.
'The dark down there is older than the town. Be rude to it anyway.'
The Commander hands over a lamp he has clearly been saving.
'If it has a name, do not fight it on the first day you hear it.'
E3PO stands at the stair until the last light of them is gone.
'I cannot follow you down. I dislike it enormously. Go.'
'Measure the grain, count the flasks, keep each other. Off with you.'
The Commander tells the newest delver one small true thing and sends them on.
'Nothing down there is owed anything by you. Remember it.'
E3PO writes the party into his book before they are out of sight.
'Four went down. I shall be wanting four.'
The Commander does not say good luck. He says the stair is kept clear, and means it as the same thing.
'Leave the heroics for the way out. It is a longer walk than you think.'
E3PO salutes the stair itself, which is either habit or manners.
'When you are tired, climb. Tired men fight badly and climb fine.'

lord_cleared: 'It had a name. It has a past tense now.'
The Commander reads the lord's name off the report and crosses it out himself.
E3PO rings the bell with no clapper. Everyone hears it.
'That one has been down there since before the wall. Well done. Properly.'
The Commander orders the gates opened wide, which is as close as he comes to celebrating.
'I have stood at this door a long while waiting for that news.'
E3PO buys the round and then stands at the back of the room, satisfied.
'Write the names of the party above the name of the thing. That is the correct order.'
The Commander goes to the stairhead and looks down for a long moment. Just checking.
'Lords come in their own order. Rest while the next is still polite enough to wait.'
E3PO tells the recruits the story that evening and gets the party's names exactly right.
'The scar is quieter tonight. Enjoy it. It will not last.'
The Commander has a stone cut for the ones who did not come back up, before the cheering stops.
'Good. Now the hard part - do not get careless on the way down next time.'
E3PO takes the broken crown, looks at it, and puts it in the guild post where the children can see it.
'That is one door the town will never have to hold again.'
The Commander sleeps four hours, which for him is a festival.
'Tell me how it went. Then tell me what nearly went wrong, which is the useful half.'
viewer_cosmetic: 'A new cloak. Good. Be visible, be findable, be alive.'
The Commander inspects the dye, says the colour's name correctly, and nods.
'A hat is not armour. I see you have reached your own conclusion.'
E3PO reads the new title off the guild board and uses it, straight-faced, all day.
'That banner wants a pole and a man. You are one of the two.'
The Commander has worn the same harness for a lifetime and admires yours anyway.
'Smart. The town likes looking at people who came back.'
E3PO straightens your collar before you walk past the gate crowd.
'Whatever you paid, the mender will want half of it. Plan for the mender.'
The Commander asks where the dye came from and remembers the trader's name.
'A pet. It may sit by the gate. It may not sit on the gate.'
'Titles are free to say and expensive to earn. Yours is said, at least.'
E3PO salutes the new colours with no trace of a joke in it, which is the joke.
'Keep the clasp oiled. Everything fails at the clasp.'
The Commander tells the watch your new name once, so they get it right the first time.
'The old cloak was fine. The new cloak is fine. You are what wears it.'
E3PO notices the thread-work, pauses, and says 'good hands made that.'
'Wear it on the wall. Finery that never leaves the chest is just a bill.'
The Commander approves. He will deny approving.
'Looking like a hero is the cheap half. I shall be watching the other half.'
rank_up: 'Promoted. Now the mistakes get expensive. Congratulations.'
The Commander says your new rank aloud at the gate, so the whole watch hears it from him first.
'You are above men now. Stand in front of them accordingly.'
E3PO signs the roll, blows on the ink, and shakes your hand like a man closing a deal.
'Rank is the town saying it trusts you. Do not make a liar of it.'
The Commander hands over the keys to a gate he will still check himself every night.
'Better pay, worse sleep. That is the arrangement.'
E3PO tells you, quietly, the one thing he wishes somebody had told him.
'You may now shout. Choose your moments; I did not, and look at me.'
The Commander steps back half a pace and lets you give the order.
'If they follow you, it is because you were there first. Always be there first.'
E3PO puts your name on the duty board in his own hand, which he does not do for everyone.
'You have outgrown the easy watch. I shall miss sending you to it.'
The Commander promotes you and immediately gives you something difficult, out of respect.
'A rank is a door you now help hold. Welcome to the hinge.'
E3PO salutes you. Properly. It takes a moment to realise what has happened.
trader_arrives: 'Open the gate. Count the carts. Count them again when they leave.'
The Commander greets the caravan master by name and asks after a child he has never met.
'Trade is a wall you cannot see. Be courteous to it.'
E3PO looks over the cargo, finds nothing wrong, and says so where the trader can hear.
'Weigh it honestly in front of me and we shall have no trouble at all.'
The Commander walks the carts in himself, which the traders take as the compliment it is.
'They came over the scar road. Give them water before you give them prices.'
E3PO declines a gift twice and accepts a cup of tea on the third attempt.
'No weapons sold inside the wall after the bell. I do not care what it fetches.'
The Commander asks the road news first and the price list second.
'Bellmire pays. Bellmire also remembers. Keep both in mind.'
E3PO posts a guard on the caravan all night and calls it hospitality.
'If they are short-weighting us, they will do it where it is dark. Light the market.'
The Commander buys nothing and inspects everything.
'Carts out at dawn. I want the gate my own again by breakfast.'
E3PO sees the caravan a mile down the road, because the first mile is the dangerous one.
drill: 'Again. The enemy will also ask you to do it again.'
The Commander drills the watch in the rain, because the rain will not wait for a dry day.
'Slower. Correct, then quick. Never quick, then wrong.'
E3PO takes the practice spear and lets three recruits try him at once, for the lesson.
'A shield wall is a conversation. Stop shouting over each other.'
The Commander walks the line and moves four men an inch each. The line looks entirely different.
'You will fight how you drilled, so drill as though you are frightened.'
E3PO counts the beat aloud until the whole yard is on it.
'Hold. Hold. Hold. Good - that was the whole battle.'
The Commander demonstrates a parry, then the mistake, then the parry again, patiently.
'Your arm hurts because it is learning. Mine hurt for a century.'
E3PO never drills the same hour two days running. Habits get doors opened at the wrong hour.
The Commander puts the worst recruit beside himself and says nothing about it.
'If you can do it tired, you can do it at night. If you can do it at night, you can do it.'
E3PO ends the drill early and nobody believes it until he has gone.
'Good. Now forget it, so your hands can remember it instead.'
The Commander drills the bucket line as hard as the shield line. He has seen which one gets used.
dispute: The Commander hears both sides at the gate, standing, because standing keeps it short.
'You are both right and it is both your faults. Split it and go home.'
E3PO judges a boundary quarrel by walking the boundary himself.
'Say it to his face in front of me, and we shall see how much of it you meant.'
The Commander has never jailed a man he could walk home instead.
'Theft in my town. Explain it to me slowly. I should like to be fair.'
E3PO returns the stolen goods personally and never says who took them.
'Debts are for the reeve. Fists are for me. Choose which this is.'
The Commander hears a drunk's grievance all the way to the end, in full harness, at midnight.
'The law in Bellmire is thin. I am thick enough to make up the difference.'
E3PO fines a man and then quietly pays half of it himself, badly hidden.
'Hit him again and the next conversation is shorter.'
The Commander writes the ruling down, so that it can be argued with later, properly.
'I do not care who started it. I care who is finishing it.'
E3PO sits the two of them down with one cup between them. It usually works.
'You will shake hands, or you will stand here with me until you would rather.'

town_life._note: Ambient Bellmire flavour as the town grows - crier calls, market and guild chatter, building news. For the desktop's town.gd if it wires a ticker; content worker never touches code. Additive; dead until wired.
crier: Grain measured, flasks counted, door kept - Bellmire stands another day!
Fresh off the river: trout, and a tale with every one.
The guild takes names at the post. Bring your own courage.
Lamps lit, walls walked, all's well - or well enough.
Another delver down the scar. Put a copper on them coming back up.
Walls walked, gates kept, and the bell has nothing to say!
Caravan on the road - bring coin or bring your back!
New names on the guild post. Read them while they are fresh.
The apothecary has flasks and the guild has holes to put them in!
Taxes measured, not guessed - the Hall says so.
Rain by evening. The crier is never wrong twice running.
Measure the grain, count the flasks, keep the door - and the crier keeps his voice!
Two up from the scar this morning, and both of them walking!
The bell has no clapper and even less to say. All's well!
Market day! Bring coin, bring elbows!
The Watch walked the wall twice and found nothing worth a second turn.
Flasks on the shelf, grain in the measure - Bellmire keeps its own accounts!
A lord came up out of the scar and went back down in pieces - hear it twice for a copper!
E3PO stood the night gate himself. Sleep easy, Bellmire.
Three down the scar before breakfast. The guild post is open and the ink is wet!
Stone on the road, masons on the wall - look lively or be built into it!
The Ford is running high. Cross at the ferry or cross at your own funeral!
Lost: one goat, answers to nothing. Found: one goat, answers to nobody!
The Hall sits at noon. Bring your grievance and bring it short!
Bandits on the west road, says the carter. Says it every week, mind.
Flasks counted twice today, on account of yesterday!
A caravan winters here, and the lanes are tight. Mind your elbows and your purse!
The night was quiet, the gate held, and the crier slept like an honest man!
New law posted at the Hall. Read it, or have it read to you at the gallows!
market: Two coppers the carp, and the carp is grinning.
Dye by the ounce - name a colour, Bellmire keeps it now.
Scarglass! Cheap, and only slightly cursed!
Boots that have walked further than you have, half off.
Ale by the jug, and the jug is honest.
Nails, hooks, and a hammer that has seen things!
Salt off the coast road - you will taste the journey.
Wool off the hill, and it still smells of the hill.
Bread this morning; bread-shaped by this afternoon.
Lamp oil! Burns slow, and you will want the slow sort.
Rope by the fathom, and it has held a man before!
Scarstone, polished - it only looks at you a little!
Candles! Burn one for the delvers, buy two for yourself!
Hooks, lines, and a river that owes you nothing!
Cheese with a crust you could roof a barn with!
Fresh ink and honest parchment - write home while you still can!
A hat that has never once been rained on. Not once!
Secondhand steel - all of it came back up. Most of it alone.
Wax and wick! Burn one for the ones still down there!
Charcoal by the sack, and the sack is nearly full!
Thread, needles, and a patch for whatever the scar did to you!
Smoked river fish - it has been through worse than you have!
Horn cups, horn combs, horn everything - we had a good year for horns!
Pickles! Older than some of my customers!
Blankets off the hill flocks, thick enough to stand up on their own!
Boots resoled while you wait, and you will wait!
Honey when the hives are ours to take it from. Today they are!
Lanterns, hooks and a long pole - everything a man needs to not go in after it!
growth: The masons raised a new course on the wall today.
A second well dug, and the queue at the first one shorter.
They are building where the fields used to stop.
The guild post has two doors now. Both kept.
The smith has an apprentice, and the apprentice has eyebrows. For now.
A proper gate, hung and swinging true.
The road out is cobbled as far as the ford.
They are putting glass in the chapel windows.
A second row of stalls, and a queue for them.
The barracks took on ten more. E3PO looked almost pleased.
The ditch is dug, the stakes are in, and the masons are measuring stone.
A new row of chimneys on the east side, all of them smoking.
They have hung a lamp at the ford. It burns all night now.
The guild post took on a clerk, and the clerk took on a queue.
A tannery, downwind - and the town voted on which wind.
The market square has flagstones where the mud was.
A second smith, and the two of them already disagree.
They are cutting a road where the fields used to stop.
They have roofed the old well, and the water tastes of less sky.
A stone granary going up by the Hall, and the masons will not say how much.
Drains under the high street. The town smells of digging instead of worse.
The chapel has a clapper on order, and opinions arriving free.
A second gate cut in the north wall, because the first one had a queue.
The guild post painted its door. The door is still kept.
A bath house, of all things, and a line outside it already.
They are laying a wharf at the Ford, long enough for two boats to argue over.
