propositions._note: Viewer-voting town laws (T4). 17 across law/taxes/militia/building/faith/outsiders. Each names a CONSEQUENCE, good and bad - a law that only helps is boring. Readable at a glance. Dead until wired.

entries.title: The Gallows Law
entries.flavour: Thieves hang, not fine. The guild says it will clear the market of cutpurses.
entries.good: Crime falls; the market feels safe to spend in.
entries.bad: The desperate turn to worse than theft, and some good hands leave town.

entries.title: Trial by the Roll
entries.flavour: Let the accused delve the scar. Come back up, and you walk free.
entries.good: Wildly popular on stream, and the dungeon runs hot.
entries.bad: The innocent die below, and the guild loses good names.

entries.title: Debtors' Pardon
entries.flavour: Wipe the slate. Come spring, no one in Bellmire owes a copper.
entries.good: The poor breathe again; loyalty climbs.
entries.bad: The lenders shut their purses, and coin stops moving.

entries.title: Raise the Grain Tithe
entries.flavour: A heavier cut of every harvest goes to the town coffers.
entries.good: The treasury swells; walls and wages get paid.
entries.bad: Full barns, thin bellies - the folk grumble, and some go hungry.

entries.title: The Free Market Charter
entries.flavour: Drop the market tolls. Any trader sells in Bellmire toll-free.
entries.good: Caravans flock in; the stalls overflow.
entries.bad: The coffers thin, and the guild's grip slips.

entries.title: Toll at the Ford
entries.flavour: A copper to cross, paid to the Ferryman, paid to the town.
entries.good: Steady coin off every crossing.
entries.bad: Traders grumble, some ford downstream, and the Ferryman is not thanked.

entries.title: Raise the Militia Levy
entries.flavour: Every household sends a hand to the wall.
entries.good: The guard doubles; raiders think twice.
entries.bad: Fewer hands in the fields - the town is safer but poorer.

entries.title: Arm the Delvers
entries.flavour: Guild steel for anyone who will hold the gate.
entries.good: A hard town to raid.
entries.bad: Armed and idle men make their own trouble.

entries.title: Night Curfew
entries.flavour: Lamps out, doors barred, the Watch walks till dawn.
entries.good: No raid slips in by night.
entries.bad: The taverns empty; the folk feel watched, not kept.

entries.title: Wall the Town
entries.flavour: Stone where the fields stop. The masons are ready and waiting.
entries.good: Bellmire holds against any raid.
entries.bad: It costs a fortune, and the harvest waits while the masons build.

entries.title: Dig the Second Well
entries.flavour: One well, long queues, and the dry months coming.
entries.good: Water for all, even in a drought.
entries.bad: The diggers want paying, and they keep hitting scarstone.

entries.title: Pave the Market Square
entries.flavour: Mud to flagstone, fit for a city.
entries.good: Traders linger; the town looks the part.
entries.bad: A whole season's coin, sunk into the ground.

entries.title: Ring the Festival
entries.flavour: A feast day on the guild's coin, and the clapperless bell rung anyway.
entries.good: Spirits soar; both loyalty and trade rise.
entries.bad: A day's work lost, and a day's coin with it.

entries.title: Tithe to the Chapel
entries.flavour: Fund the temple and light every candle.
entries.good: The faithful are glad; the sick are tended.
entries.bad: Coin the walls could have used.

entries.title: Open the Gates to Refugees
entries.flavour: Folk fleeing the scar-lands crowd the Ford by the hundred.
entries.good: New hands for the fields and the wall.
entries.bad: More mouths to feed - and sickness travels with them.

entries.title: Hire the Sellswords
entries.flavour: Coin for blades that answer to gold, not the guild.
entries.good: Hard muscle for the hard floors.
entries.bad: They stay bought only as long as you keep paying.

entries.title: Shut the Border
entries.flavour: No stranger past the Ford without the guild's word.
entries.good: No raider walks in wearing a traveller's coat.
entries.bad: Trade withers, and the town turns inward and small.

entries.title: The Honest Measure
entries.flavour: Every weight in the market checked at the Hall, and stamped, or smashed.
entries.good: Buyers trust the stalls; market takings and the town cut both rise.
entries.bad: The sharper traders take their carts to an easier road, and stalls stand empty a while.

entries.title: Blood Price
entries.flavour: A killing is settled in coin paid to the family, not in rope.
entries.good: Feuds end at the Hall instead of in the street; fewer good hands are lost.
entries.bad: A rich man can afford a murder, and everyone in town can do the sum.

entries.title: Chain Them to the Wall
entries.flavour: Taken bandits work the wall instead of hanging from it.
entries.good: Building goes faster and costs the town nothing in wages.
entries.bad: Armed men guarding chained men; now and then a chain comes off at night.

entries.title: The Delver's Tithe
entries.flavour: One part in ten of everything carried up the scar, paid at the post.
entries.good: The treasury fills whenever the dungeon runs hot.
entries.bad: Delvers hide the best of it, and some sell to the Ford instead of the guild.

entries.title: Hearth Tax
entries.flavour: Every chimney in Bellmire pays, counted from the wall on a cold morning.
entries.good: Steady coin that does not care whether the dungeon pays out this week.
entries.bad: The poorest let their fires go out to go uncounted, and the winter takes some of them.

entries.title: The Scarglass Levy
entries.flavour: Tax what comes out of the scar as glass, not as gold.
entries.good: The oddities pay their way, and the apothecary gets first refusal on stock.
entries.bad: Scarglass goes under the counter; smuggling takes root at the Ford.

entries.title: Drill Every Seventh Day
entries.flavour: Every able hand in the yard one day in seven. E3PO calls the time.
entries.good: The militia holds a line instead of breaking; raid losses drop sharply.
entries.bad: A day in seven out of the fields and workshops - everything else comes slower.

entries.title: The Night Horn
entries.flavour: A horn hung in every quarter, and a standing order to blow it first and ask after.
entries.good: The town turns out fast; raids are met at the gate rather than in the square.
entries.bad: False alarms most weeks, and a town that sleeps badly works badly.

entries.title: Muster the Farmhands
entries.flavour: The outlying holdings send one hand each to the garrison for the season.
entries.good: The garrison stands at full strength through the dangerous months.
entries.bad: Harvest comes in short-handed, and the holdings remember who asked.

entries.title: Roof the Market
entries.flavour: Timber and tile over the square, so market day happens whatever the sky does.
entries.good: Market day never cancels; trade income steadies across the whole year.
entries.bad: Costly, and a roofed square burns as one thing instead of twenty.

entries.title: Dig the Drains
entries.flavour: Stone drains under the streets, downhill, away from the well.
entries.good: Sickness drops and the town stops stinking in summer; growth comes easier.
entries.bad: Months of open trench through the middle of everything, and the cost of every yard of it.

entries.title: Raise a Granary
entries.flavour: A stone granary by the Hall, kept full against a bad year.
entries.good: A failed harvest or a burned field no longer means a hungry winter.
entries.bad: Grain sits idle that could have been sold, and a full granary is a target worth raiding.

entries.title: Hang a Clapper in the Bell
entries.flavour: The bell has rung without one since the tower went up. The chapel wants it finished.
entries.good: A bell that carries - the town hears a raid called from any field it works.
entries.bad: Some swear the bell was better unfinished, and the old families take it badly.

entries.title: Bring the Delvers Home
entries.flavour: The town pays to carry its dead up out of the scar and bury them in daylight.
entries.good: Delvers go down easier knowing it; the guild post never wants for names.
entries.bad: A steady drain of coin, and parties that turn back carrying a body instead of loot.

entries.title: Winter the Caravans
entries.flavour: Let the road traders keep their carts inside the wall until the thaw.
entries.good: Goods and coin stay in Bellmire all winter, and the spring road opens from here.
entries.bad: Crowded lanes, strained stores, and outsiders who learn the inside of the wall by heart.

disasters._note: Natural disasters (D34). For each: begin (Chronicle line), during (lines while it lasts), pass (line when it ends), cost (plain statement of what it should cost the town, for the desktop to implement). Dead until wired.
disasters._note_variants: Added C-cycle 11: begin_alt and pass_alt (arrays) sit beside begin and pass on EVERY disaster, and during is widened to 8 lines each. begin/pass are unchanged and still the single canonical line - a picker may roll begin_alt/pass_alt instead so a second volcano does not read word for word like the first. Additive; dead until wired.

volcano.begin: The mountain above the scar wakes - ash on the wind, and the sky goes copper.
during: Ash falls on Bellmire; the sun is a dull coin behind the smoke.
The river runs grey, and the fish float up dead.
Cinders tick off the roof-tiles all night; nobody opens a shutter.
The crier reads the day's news through a cloth over his mouth.
The ash drifts into the grain store through a gap nobody knew was there.
Sheep come down off the high pasture coughing, and do not go back up.
The chapel bell rings muffled, packed with grey.
Children write their names in the ash on the shutters. By morning it has written over them.
A cart leaves two clean ruts in the grey, and nothing else does.
The guild post sells cloth masks and is out of them by noon.
Lamps are lit at midday; the copper sky gives nothing to work by.
Ash sits a finger deep on the chapel steps and is swept twice a day.
Grey settles on the market bread, and the bread sells anyway.
The high pasture is gone under ash; the shepherds bring everything down.
Ash falls like grey snow and the cookfires are put out to save the air.
The mountain speaks again and every bell in Bellmire answers it badly.
Carts queue at the Ford with everything a household can lift.
The water butts are skimmed twice a day and still run grey.
A roof goes in under the weight of its own ash, and nobody was under it.
The crier's voice carries badly; the ash eats it before the far side of the square.
The guild post weighs ash out of the grain and charges for honest weight.
Every doorstep is swept, and every doorstep is grey again by dusk.
The forge works blind, the smoke of its own making lost in the bigger smoke.
Bellmire counts the flasks early this week, because the lamps burn all day.
volcano.pass: The mountain settles. Ash greys every roof, but the air clears.
volcano.cost: A buried harvest and sickened livestock; the worst-hit district must be rebuilt.
begin_alt: Grit on the tongue before dawn - the mountain is awake, and the sky turns copper.
The mountain clears its throat. Ash comes down on Bellmire like slow snow.
Ash on the wind out of the high country. Shutter the stores.
The mountain wakes above the scar, and the first ash reaches the square by noon.
Copper sky, grit in the water butt. The mountain has started.
Smoke stands over the high country in a column, and the column is leaning this way.
The mountain opens, and the sky over Bellmire turns the colour of a bruise.
Ash on the wind before dawn - the mountain has decided something.
The high country lights from underneath, and the wind brings the first grey.
Thunder with no cloud. The mountain is clearing its throat again.
The water butts skin over grey before breakfast. It has started.
A red seam opens on the mountain's shoulder and the sky closes over it.
The mountain lifts a column of smoke, and the column points at Bellmire.
First ash by first light. The crier is told to speak through cloth.
The high pasture goes under grey before the shepherds are awake.
The mountain burns somewhere inside itself, and Bellmire gets the smoke.
pass_alt: The mountain goes quiet. Bellmire shovels grey off its roofs and breathes clean.
The ashfall stops. Every rooftop wears a winter nobody ordered.
The sky loses its copper. The sweeping will take a month.
The column over the mountain thins and comes apart. It is finished.
The last grey flake lands. Bellmire starts at the roofs and works down.
The air comes clean again, one street at a time.
The mountain quiets. Ash lies a thumb deep on every roof that is left.
It is over. The town digs itself out grey to the knee.
The seam on the mountain closes. The shovels come out and stay out.
No new grey since dawn. Bellmire counts its roofs and starts lifting.
The smoke stands straight again, then not at all. It is done.
The sky lets the sun through, thin and ordinary, and the town cheers it.
The ash stops. Every gutter in town is packed and every gutter gets dug.
The mountain banks its fire. Grey to the knee, and all of it to move.
Clean air off the river at last. The grey goes back up the hill in carts.
It is over. The grain store is opened and the counting starts.

The crater cools. Scarglass in the rim, and a queue to get at it.
The burning stops. What fell is worth more than what it broke.
It is over. The crater is roped off and then immediately not.
The ground stops smoking. The guild post sets a price on scarglass by noon.
The fires are out. Bellmire is poorer by a district and richer by a crater.
Settled. The crater glitters, and the architect wants a look.
The last flame is beaten out. The digging starts the same hour.
Done. A hole where the orchard was, and glass worth a fortune in it.

scarstorm.begin: The scar flares, and wild magic rolls up out of the dungeon mouth and over the town.
during: Every spell cast in Bellmire goes wrong; the lamps burn strange colours.
The livestock speak for a heartbeat, and the well runs uphill.
The apothecary corks everything and sits on the box.
A delver's lamp burns green, and the dark leans in to look.
A door opens onto a different room than it did this morning.
Every candle in the chapel burns blue and will not be put out.
A cooper's barrel fills itself with river water, and nobody touches it.
The casters sit it out, hands in their laps, useless and insulted.
Shadows fall the wrong way across the square, and nobody mentions it.
A hedge flowers out of season, all at once, and then forgets.
The chapel bell rings a note that is not one of its own.
A delver's blade goes cold enough to burn the hand holding it.
The crier reads his notice twice and it says different things.
Birds fly one circle over the scar and will not break it.
The scar breathes out, and the air in the lower streets goes wrong.
Lamps burn purple at the scar's edge and the Watch pulls back a street.
Nothing comes out of the scar. That is the part that frightens people.
No spell holds while it lasts; casters stand in the square with nothing to offer.
A house is a slightly different shape by morning and will not be argued with.
The guild post's weights read differently every hour and are set aside.
Somebody comes out of the storm scar-touched, and it is not yet clear which way.
The bell with no clapper rings clean, once, and will not do it again.
The lamps burn colours and the oil is spent at twice the rate.
Nobody walks near the scar's mouth, and the watch is doubled anyway.
scarstorm.pass: The scar quiets. The magic settles, mostly, and the town tallies what changed.
scarstorm.cost: Spellcasters are useless while it lasts; random buildings warp, and a few folk are scar-touched for good or ill.
begin_alt: The scar flares. Wild magic rolls out of the dungeon mouth and over the roofs.
The scar breathes out, and what it breathes is not air.
Magic comes up out of the scar in a wave, looking for somewhere to land.
Light comes up out of the dungeon mouth and spills over the roofs.
The scar flares, and every caster in Bellmire feels the floor go out from under them.
Wild magic comes up the scar the way water comes up a well-shaft.
The scar is loud tonight, and the colour over it is not a colour.
Something turns over down in the scar, and the town feels it in the teeth.
The scar flares, and wild magic rolls up out of the dark and over the roofs.
The air goes wrong. Every caster in Bellmire feels it at once.
Light climbs out of the scar and spreads across the town like weather.
The scar opens its mouth and breathes magic over Bellmire.
Spells go sideways in the square. The storm is up.
Colour runs across the sky that no sky should have.
The dungeon mouth glows, and the glow comes up and out.
The scar misfires on everything at once, and the town is inside it.
pass_alt: The scar quiets. The magic settles - mostly - and the tally begins.
It passes. Bellmire checks what changed, and what changed back.
The wave rolls off. Two or three folk are scar-touched now, for good or ill.
The light sinks back down the scar. Most of what it touched comes back.
It settles. The casters try a small spell, and the small spell behaves.
The strangeness drains off, leaving two warped roofs and one very lucky man.
The scar quiets. The lamps burn honest yellow again.
It settles. Whatever that was has gone back down.
The light sinks back into the scar. Spells behave again.
The storm drains away downward. The casters test a candle flame and breathe.
The air comes right. What it warped stays warped.
It is over. A few folk came out of it changed, and they keep it to themselves.
The glow goes out of the sky. The apothecary starts her list of oddities.
The scar closes its mouth. Bellmire inventories what is no longer square.
Done. Two doors in the low district now open onto the wrong rooms.
The storm passes down into the dark. The chapel rings the all-clear.

flood.begin: The thaw comes all at once. The river climbs the banks, and keeps climbing.
during: The low district is ankle-deep, then knee-deep.
The Ford is gone under brown water; no crossing today.
The grain store is moved up a floor by every pair of hands in town.
Boats in the lane where carts should be, and someone fishing out of a window.
The Ford is gone - only the posts show where it was.
Stores go up to the Keep a sack at a time, through knee-deep water.
A hen coop sails past the chapel with the hens still aboard.
The Watch mark the water on the gatepost each hour. The marks keep climbing.
The chapel keeps the pews stacked and the floor under an inch of river.
The low district moves upstairs and lives there.
The bridge posts are all that show of the road to the Ford.
A cellar gives up its stores in a slow brown stream.
Fish are taken in the lane, which is funny for a day and then is not.
The gatehouse step is the measure now, and everybody checks it.
The lower streets take water to the knee and then to the waist.
Boats work the market square, which nobody finds funny.
Grain goes up to the Keep sack by sack, by a line that does not stop.
The low district is moved upstairs, one household helping the next.
The grain store's bottom row is lost and counted as lost out loud.
Boats work the lanes where carts worked last week.
The traders stand on the far bank and shout their prices across.
The chapel floor is under water and the service is held on the steps.
The well is fouled by the river and roped off for drinking.
Everything that can be lifted has been lifted; the rest is being watched.
flood.pass: The water drops back, leaving mud in every doorway - but the town held.
flood.cost: Riverside buildings and stores ruined; the Ford and its trade shut until the river falls.
begin_alt: The thaw comes all at once. The river climbs the bank and does not stop.
The river is over the low fields by noon and over the lane by dark.
Water in the doorways - the Ford has given up being a ford.
The thaw arrives in one night, and the river has the low fields by morning.
The river climbs the bank, then the lane, then the step.
Brown water at the Ford, moving far too fast to cross.
The river comes over the bank at the Ford and keeps coming.
Rain upriver for a week, and Bellmire is downriver.
The river climbs the bank and keeps the habit.
Brown water over the low lane before anyone has moved a sack.
The thaw comes down all at once and the river takes the low district.
The Ford goes under, and the trade goes under with it.
Water in the doorways by dark, and rising by lamplight.
The river is in the fields, then the lanes, then the front rooms.
The millrace runs backward, which is the first warning anyone heeds.
The river comes up the steps of the chapel and keeps coming.
pass_alt: The water drops back. Mud in every doorway, and the town held.
The river goes home. It left most of its bed in Bellmire's front rooms.
The flood falls away. The Ford shows its posts again, and the trade with them.
The river falls back inside its banks and leaves the mud as rent.
The water goes. Every doorway in the low district needs a shovel.
The Ford shows its stones again, and the first cart over is cheered.
The water goes down and leaves the river's silt in every ground-floor room.
It drains. The smell will be with the lower streets for a month.
The river goes back inside its banks. Mud everywhere else.
The water falls. The Ford shows its posts and the carts queue up.
It drains away. Every ground floor in the low district is shovelled out.
The river retreats and leaves the town a thumb of silt as a souvenir.
Down at last. The grain store counts what got wet and what did not.
The flood lets go. The Ford opens and the trade comes back thirsty.
The water is off the lanes. The doors are left open to dry.
Over. The mud is scraped into the river that brought it.

blight.begin: A black rot is in the grain - it came up in one field and did not stop there.
during: Whole rows are cut and burned before the rot can walk to the next field.
The miller turns away sack after sack, and says nothing, which is worse.
The rot shows black at the stalk and climbs from there.
Field hands burn their gloves at the end of the day, just in case.
Bread goes up a copper, then another, and the baker stops apologising.
The guild post buys grain from downriver at a price it will not read aloud.
A farmer stands at his field edge all afternoon doing nothing at all.
They plough the worst acre under and sow nothing in it.
The smoke of burning rows hangs over the fields all week.
Seed grain is set aside and guarded, because next year is in the sack.
A field is written off at noon and burned by dusk.
The baker mixes in what he can and calls it bread, generously.
Hands are scrubbed at the field gate before anyone walks home.
Downriver grain comes up the road under guard and is counted twice.
The fields go black in patches that spread while you watch them.
They burn one field to save the next and argue about it for years after.
The apothecary tests the grain and will not say what she found.
Infected fields are burned, deliberately, with the whole town watching.
Grain prices climb at the market and are read out anyway.
The seed corn is locked and a guard is put on the lock.
Traders come upriver with grain and name a price nobody likes.
The reeve walks the rows daily, marking what is still clean.
Bread is smaller this week and will be smaller next week.
The stores are measured twice, by two different people, in public.
blight.pass: The blight burns out at the field edge. What is left of the harvest comes in early.
blight.cost: Most of the standing harvest is lost; food prices climb and the stores do not refill this season.
begin_alt: Black rot in the grain. It started in one field and did not stay there.
The harvest has something in it, and the something is spreading.
A blight walks the fields row by row, taking its time.
The grain blackens at the stalk in one field, and then in the next.
A rot comes up in the barley and starts to travel.
The harvest has gone wrong in a way the old farmers recognise.
Something is in the crop, and it moved from one furrow to the next overnight.
The barley goes grey at the edges, field by field.
Black rot in the grain, and it did not stay in the one field.
The standing crop goes dark at the root and spreads along the rows.
A rot in the ears. The reeve walks the fields and comes back quiet.
The grain is black where it should be gold, field after field.
Something is in the crop, and it is in all of the crop by week's end.
The blight shows up at the field edge and works inward.
The harvest turns dark on the stalk and nobody can stop it.
Rot in the grain, and the barns are told to expect less.
pass_alt: The blight stops at the field edge. What is left comes in early and thin.
The rot burns out. Bellmire salvages whatever the fire did not reach.
It ends. The barns take a half-harvest and are told to make it do.
The last blackened row burns, and the rot has nowhere left to go.
The blight stops. What came in is thin, early and ours.
It burns out at the hedge. The barns take half of what was promised.
It stops at the burned line. What is left is harvested nervously.
The blight dies back. So has a third of the harvest.
The rot burns out with the stubble. Next year's seed is clean.
The blight is done. The fields are bare and the ground is sound.
It is over. What was saved is counted and the price settles.
The last black field is burned. The smoke smells like a bad year ending.
The rot stops at the fallow. The seed corn is clean and guarded.
The blight dies with the frost. The barns are short but honest.
Finished. The reeve walks clean rows and says so in the square.
The fields are cleared and limed. The next sowing is already argued over.

coldsnap.begin: The cold comes early and hard - the Ford freezes over in a night.
during: Firewood costs what wine cost last week, and the queue for it is longer.
The Watch walk in pairs now, because one man alone stops moving.
The Ford is a road now, and nobody trusts it enough to use it.
The forge is the warmest room in Bellmire, and the smith charges for the privilege.
Water freezes in the bucket between the well and the door.
Caravans turn back at the hill, and the market has empty boards.
They bring the lambs indoors and share the floor with them.
The chapel takes in whoever has no fire, and the chapel is full.
Nails of ice hang off every eave, long enough to be dangerous.
The well head is thawed each morning with a kettle.
One oven bakes for the whole street, to save the wood.
The garrison drills indoors and complains, which keeps it warm.
Cattle breath stands in the byre like smoke that will not leave.
Two nights running, nobody goes further than the next door.
The river takes a skin of ice and the ferry stops for the first time in years.
Firewood doubles in price by noon and the Watch stands over the woodpile.
The old and the young are moved into the Keep hall together.
Livestock is brought indoors and lives among the household.
Building stops: the mortar will not set and nobody pretends it will.
The Ford is ice, so the trade is ice too - nothing moves either way.
Firewood is rationed and the rationing is read out by the crier.
The wells are broken open with a mallet each morning.
Work in Craft Row halts; the forge is the warmest room in Bellmire.
The chapel is full because the chapel is heated.
coldsnap.pass: The thaw comes. The Ford runs again, and Bellmire counts who it kept.
coldsnap.cost: Livestock lost and work stopped: building, trade and the fields all halt until the thaw.
begin_alt: The cold comes early and hard, and the Ford freezes over in a night.
Winter arrives a month ahead of schedule and makes itself at home.
Ice on the inside of the shutters by morning. This will be a bad one.
The Ford freezes in a night, and the cold is not finished.
Winter comes early and hard, and the firewood price rises with the sun.
Cold enough by dusk that the ground rings underfoot.
The cold arrives overnight and takes the fen's water with it.
Frost on the inside of the shutters by morning - this one means to stay.
The cold arrives early and hard, and the Ford freezes in a night.
Ice on the inside of the shutters by morning.
The river stops moving. So does most of Bellmire.
A cold out of the high country that stops work where it finds it.
The Ford is ice thick enough to walk and too thin to trust.
The frost comes down before the harvest is fully in.
Cold enough that the mortar will not set and the masons go home.
The wells skin over. The firewood is counted like grain.
pass_alt: The thaw comes. The Ford runs, and Bellmire counts who it kept.
The ice gives up. Water moves again, and so does the town.
The cold breaks. The first cart over the Ford gets a cheer it did not expect.
The ice on the Ford breaks up and goes downriver in plates.
The thaw arrives. The eaves drip all day and nobody minds the mud.
It warms. The chapel empties, and the fires go out one at a time.
The thaw comes. The town counts who came through, and how much wood is left.
It breaks, and the river runs again. Nobody cheers; it is too early for that.
The thaw. Water moves in the river and the Ford is a ford again.
The cold lets go. The scaffolds fill up with masons by noon.
Ice off the river, mud in the lanes, and everybody glad of the mud.
The frost breaks. The building starts where it stopped.
Warm wind off the water. The town stretches and gets back to it.
The thaw comes. The lost livestock is counted and the rest turned out.
The river runs. The traders come down it the same day.
Over. The firewood that is left is stacked for next time.

disasters._note_variants_c24: Widened C-cycle 24: every disaster's begin_alt 8 -> 16, pass_alt 8 -> 16 and during 17 -> 24, so a second volcano, fire or flood on the same stream does not read word for word like the first. begin, pass and cost are UNCHANGED - cost is still the single precise statement the desktop implements from. Additive; dead until wired.

events._note: Random world events (D33): bandit and monster camps that stand until cleared, and a wandering boss scaled to the town's level. Dead until wired.
events._note_variants: Added C-cycle 11: 3 more bandit camps (4 -> 7), 3 more monster camps (3 -> 6) in the same key shape, and appears_alt / while_alt / cleared_alt on wandering_boss - there is only one wandering boss, so its three lines would otherwise repeat verbatim every time it walks. Additive; dead until wired.

bandit_camps.name: The Gallows Oak
bandit_camps.appears: Red Harl's lot have taken the west road. No caravan reaches the Ford unbled.
bandit_camps.while: Trade caravans are robbed; the market runs short and prices climb.
bandit_camps.cleared: Red Harl hangs from his own Gallows Oak. The west road is open again.
appears_alt: Red Harl is back under the Gallows Oak, and the west road has gone quiet the wrong way.
The west road has a toll again, and Red Harl set it. No caravan reaches the Ford unbled.
There are new ropes on the Gallows Oak. Red Harl's lot hold the west road.
A caravan came in short a driver and a wheel. Red Harl holds the west road.
while_alt: Caravans come in robbed or not at all; the market runs short and the prices climb.
Every west-road caravan is bled. Stalls go empty and what is left costs more.
Trade bleeds on the west road - short stock in the market, and a higher price on all of it.
The caravans pay Red Harl first. The market pays for it in empty shelves and dear goods.
cleared_alt: Red Harl hangs from his own oak. The west road carries caravans, not corpses.
The Gallows Oak earns its name. The west road is open.
Red Harl's lot are scattered off the west road. The next caravan comes in whole.
The oak is used properly at last. Trade runs the west road again.

bandit_camps.name: The Mire Nest
bandit_camps.appears: Sedge the Toll holds the fen path and taxes everyone who is not her.
bandit_camps.while: Every trader by the fen pays Sedge first; the town's cut shrinks.
bandit_camps.cleared: Sedge the Toll pays her own toll at last. The fen path clears.
appears_alt: Sedge the Toll is back on the fen path, and she still taxes everyone who is not her.
There is a rope across the fen path and Sedge the Toll holding the end of it.
The fen path has a tollkeeper nobody appointed. Sedge is in the Mire Nest again.
Traders come in light and say the same name: Sedge the Toll.
while_alt: Every trader by the fen pays Sedge before he pays Bellmire; the town's cut shrinks.
The fen trade is taxed twice. Sedge takes hers first and the town takes what is left.
Sedge's toll comes off the top of every fen crossing; the town's share thins by the day.
What the fen path earns, Sedge earns. The town's cut falls while the Nest stands.
cleared_alt: Sedge the Toll pays her own toll. The fen path is free.
The Mire Nest is pulled apart. Nobody is charging for the fen now.
Sedge's rope comes down off the fen path. So does Sedge.
The fen path is honest again. The town's cut comes back whole.

bandit_camps.name: The Burnt Mill
bandit_camps.appears: Cob Ashfoot's raiders have holed up in the burnt mill, firing a field a night to keep the town afraid.
bandit_camps.while: A field burns most nights; harvest and morale both drop.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Burnt Mill burns one last time. Cob Ashfoot runs, and keeps running.
appears_alt: Smoke off the burnt mill again. Cob Ashfoot is firing a field a night to keep the town afraid.
Cob Ashfoot is back in the burnt mill, and the sky over the fields is orange by midnight.
A field went up in the dark and nobody lit it. Cob Ashfoot holds the mill.
The burnt mill has lights in it. Cob Ashfoot's raiders are in residence.
while_alt: A field burns most nights; the harvest comes in short and the town sleeps badly.
Another field a night. Harvest drops, and so does every face in the market.
The fields burn by turns - less grain at the measure and less heart in the town.
Cob takes a field a night. Harvest and morale both go with it.
cleared_alt: The burnt mill burns one last time. Cob Ashfoot runs and keeps running.
Cob Ashfoot is out of the mill and out of the valley. The fields keep their fire to the hearth.
The mill is ash and the fields are not. Cob Ashfoot is gone.
No lights in the burnt mill tonight. The harvest comes in whole.

bandit_camps.name: Scarside Camp
bandit_camps.appears: The Weasel's crew squat at the scar's edge, robbing the delvers who climb out.
bandit_camps.while: Returning delvers are waylaid; their gold and loot never reach Bellmire.
bandit_camps.cleared: Scarside Camp is cleared. Delvers come up to friends now, not knives.
appears_alt: The Weasel's crew are at the scar's edge again, robbing whoever climbs out.
Scarside Camp is up. The Weasel waits where the delvers surface.
A delver came up rich and walked in poor. The Weasel holds the scar's edge.
There are knives at the lip of the scar, and The Weasel counting behind them.
while_alt: Delvers are waylaid coming up; their gold and loot never reach Bellmire.
Every climb out is taxed in blood. What the scar gives, Scarside Camp keeps.
The Weasel takes it at the lip - the delve pays and the town sees none of it.
Loot stops at the scar's edge. Nothing a delver earns gets as far as the gate.
cleared_alt: Scarside Camp is cleared. Delvers come up to friends now, not knives.
The Weasel is pulled off the scar's edge. The climb out is safe.
Nothing waits at the lip but daylight. Scarside Camp is finished.
The Weasel runs out of patience and throat. Loot reaches the gate again.

bandit_camps.name: The Drover's Rest
bandit_camps.appears: Juno Blackhand has taken the drovers' inn on the north road and left the sign hanging.
bandit_camps.while: Livestock driven to market never arrive; the pens stand empty on market day.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Drover's Rest changes hands again. Juno Blackhand does not leave with it.
appears_alt: Juno Blackhand holds the drovers' inn on the north road, and left the sign hanging.
The Drover's Rest has new keepers. Juno Blackhand took it with the beer still in the cask.
No drover has come down the north road in days. Juno Blackhand is why.
There is smoke from the Drover's Rest and nobody paying for a bed. Juno Blackhand is in.
while_alt: Livestock driven to market never arrive; the pens stand empty on market day.
The herds go up the north road and stop there. Market day opens to bare pens.
Juno takes the beasts before the town sees them - empty pens, and no meat at the measure.
Nothing on four legs gets past the Rest. The market pens hold air.
cleared_alt: The Drover's Rest changes hands again. Juno Blackhand does not leave with it.
Juno Blackhand is taken out of the Rest. The herds come down the north road.
The sign still hangs. The man who hung it does too.
The Drover's Rest serves drovers. The pens fill by market day.

bandit_camps.name: The Quarry Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Old Peck's lot have moved into the worked-out quarry and are selling Bellmire its own stone back.
bandit_camps.while: Cut stone and lime go missing; building in town stalls for want of either.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Quarry Camp is emptied out. The stone comes down the road at an honest price.
appears_alt: Old Peck's lot are in the worked-out quarry, selling Bellmire its own stone back.
The old quarry has men in it again, and they are not masons. Old Peck is there.
The stone cart came in empty and expensive. Old Peck holds the quarry.
Old Peck has moved into the quarry and set his own price on what the town already owns.
while_alt: Cut stone and lime go missing; building in town stalls for want of either.
No stone, no lime - whatever Bellmire is raising stops where it stands.
The quarry's take goes to Old Peck. The scaffolds stand idle.
Stone and lime both vanish on the road. Every build in town waits.
cleared_alt: The Quarry Camp is emptied out. The stone comes down the road at an honest price.
Old Peck is walked out of the quarry. The masons have their stone.
The quarry belongs to the town again - and so does the stone in it.
Old Peck sells nothing further. Building starts where it stopped.

bandit_camps.name: The Lampless Road
bandit_camps.appears: Wick Harrow's crew put out the road lamps one by one, and work the dark they made.
bandit_camps.while: Nobody travels after dusk; the night trade stops and the Ford shuts early.
bandit_camps.cleared: The lamps burn the whole length of the road again. Wick Harrow walks it in chains.
appears_alt: Wick Harrow's crew are putting out the road lamps again, and working the dark they make.
Three lamps dark on the road tonight. Wick Harrow is back at it.
The road has gone black a mile at a time. Wick Harrow holds the dark end of it.
Someone is harvesting the lamp oil and the travellers both. Wick Harrow.
while_alt: Nobody travels after dusk; the night trade stops and the Ford shuts early.
The road is dark and empty after sundown - no night trade, and the Ford closes its doors.
Dusk ends the day's trade now. The Ford bolts up early and takes less.
After dark the road belongs to Wick. The night trade is finished and the Ford shuts.
cleared_alt: The lamps burn the whole length of the road again. Wick Harrow walks it in chains.
Every lamp lit, end to end. Wick Harrow is carried past them.
The dark is given back to the sky. The Ford keeps its late hours.
Wick Harrow's crew are out of the dark and into the light of a cell.

bandit_camps.name: The Weir Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Marek Two-Coin has fortified the old weir and charges the river for using itself.
bandit_camps.while: River trade pays twice; the Ford's takings fall while the weir stands.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Weir Camp is broken open. The river runs toll-free again.
appears_alt: Marek Two-Coin has the old weir fortified, and charges the river for using itself.
There are palings on the old weir and Marek Two-Coin behind them.
The barges came up paying twice. Marek Two-Coin holds the weir.
Marek Two-Coin is back on the weir, collecting with both hands.
while_alt: River trade pays twice; the Ford's takings fall while the weir stands.
Every barge is charged at the weir first - the Ford takes less for the same traffic.
Marek skims the river before Bellmire does. The Ford's books thin out.
Two tolls on one river. The Ford's share drops while the Weir Camp holds.
cleared_alt: The Weir Camp is broken open. The river runs toll-free again.
Marek Two-Coin is taken off the weir with neither coin. The barges pay once.
The palings come off the weir. The Ford's takings come back.
One toll on the river now, and it is the town's.

bandit_camps.name: The Ashen Barrow
bandit_camps.appears: Grell the Patient has dug into the barrow mound and watches the market road out of it.
bandit_camps.while: Market-bound carts are picked off; stalls stand empty on market day.
bandit_camps.cleared: The barrow is emptied of the living. Grell the Patient stays behind in it.
appears_alt: Grell the Patient has dug into the barrow mound and watches the market road out of it.
There is a hole in the barrow and eyes in the hole. Grell the Patient is waiting.
Grell the Patient is in the Ashen Barrow again, and he can wait longer than the town can.
The market road has a watcher nobody hired. Grell is in the mound.
while_alt: Market-bound carts are picked off; stalls stand empty on market day.
The carts do not arrive. Market day opens half-stalled.
Grell takes them one cart at a time - and the market shows the gaps.
Every cart for market is a cart for Grell. The stalls stand bare.
cleared_alt: The barrow is emptied of the living. Grell the Patient stays behind in it.
Grell ran out of patience first. The market road carries carts.
The Ashen Barrow is sealed with its proper tenants. Market day fills up.
Grell waits in the barrow permanently now. The stalls are stocked.

bandit_camps.name: The Hollow Stand
bandit_camps.appears: Ivett Crow's archers hold the wood where the road bends, and they do not miss twice.
bandit_camps.while: Couriers and tax carts are lost at the bend; news and coin both arrive late or not at all.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Hollow Stand is cleared. The road bends past nothing worse than trees.
appears_alt: Ivett Crow's archers hold the wood at the road's bend, and they do not miss twice.
The bend has gone quiet. Ivett Crow's bows are in the Hollow Stand.
A courier's horse came in without a courier. Ivett Crow holds the bend.
There are arrows in the bend-post again. The Hollow Stand is manned.
while_alt: Couriers and tax carts are lost at the bend; news and coin both arrive late or not at all.
Nothing gets round the bend - the post stops and the tax carts with it.
News ages on the road and the coin never finishes the journey.
The bend eats couriers. Word and money both come late, or not.
cleared_alt: The Hollow Stand is cleared. The road bends past nothing worse than trees.
Ivett Crow misses once, and once is enough. The post runs.
The wood at the bend is emptied of bowmen. Coin and word arrive on time.
Ivett Crow comes out of the Stand with her string cut. The road is open.

bandit_camps.name: The Shepherd's Fold
bandit_camps.appears: Dunn Halfhand has taken the high fold and keeps whatever flock he finds in it.
bandit_camps.while: Wool and mutton stop coming down off the hills; the cloth trade and the tavern both feel it.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Fold changes shepherd. Dunn Halfhand leaves with a quarter hand and no flock.
appears_alt: Dunn Halfhand has taken the high fold and keeps whatever flock he finds in it.
The high fold has a shepherd who shears other men's sheep. Dunn Halfhand.
No flock has come down off the hills this week. Dunn Halfhand holds the fold.
Dunn Halfhand is in the Shepherd's Fold, counting a flock he never raised.
while_alt: Wool and mutton stop coming down off the hills; the cloth trade and the tavern both feel it.
No wool, no mutton. The weavers slow and the tavern's pot goes thin.
The hills send nothing down. Cloth gets dear and the tavern serves less.
Dunn keeps the flocks. The cloth trade and the kitchen both run short.
cleared_alt: The Fold changes shepherd. Dunn Halfhand leaves with a quarter hand and no flock.
Dunn Halfhand is driven off the high fold. The flocks come down.
The fold holds sheep and no thieves. Wool and mutton come in again.
Dunn counts to nine now. The hills send their flocks down.

bandit_camps.name: The Lime Kiln
bandit_camps.appears: Mad Tibb's crew sleep in the lime kiln and come out white as ghosts to work the road.
bandit_camps.while: Lime and mortar never reach the masons; whatever Bellmire is building stops where it stands.
bandit_camps.cleared: The kiln is cold and empty. Mad Tibb is walked back to town the colour of chalk.
appears_alt: Mad Tibb's crew sleep in the lime kiln and come out white as ghosts to work the road.
There are white men on the road at dusk. Mad Tibb is in the kiln again.
The lime cart was taken by something that looked dead and laughed. Mad Tibb.
Mad Tibb has the lime kiln, and the chalk on his crew is not the worst thing on them.
while_alt: Lime and mortar never reach the masons; whatever Bellmire is building stops where it stands.
No lime comes in. The mortar runs out and the walls stop at the course they are on.
The masons have stone and nothing to set it with. Building halts.
Mortar fails first, then the build. Nothing rises while Tibb holds the kiln.
cleared_alt: The kiln is cold and empty. Mad Tibb is walked back to town the colour of chalk.
Mad Tibb comes out of the kiln for the last time. The lime carts run.
The Lime Kiln is cleared. The masons set stone again.
Tibb's crew are washed, chained and done. Mortar reaches the walls.

bandit_camps.name: The Sunken Boat
bandit_camps.appears: Hask has swamped a boat across the narrows and robs whoever stops to haul it clear.
bandit_camps.while: The narrows are blocked; barges wait, and what they carry spoils in the hold.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Sunken Boat burns to the waterline. Hask swims for the far bank and is met on it.
appears_alt: Hask has swamped a boat across the narrows and robs whoever stops to haul it clear.
There is a hull across the narrows that did not sink by accident. Hask put it there.
The narrows are blocked and the bank is watched. Hask is working the river.
A barge crew went to clear a wreck and came back with nothing. Hask's wreck.
while_alt: The narrows are blocked; barges wait, and what they carry spoils in the hold.
Nothing passes the narrows. The barges sit and the cargo turns.
The river queues at the wreck - goods rot in the hold while they wait.
Barges stack up at the narrows and their loads go bad where they lie.
cleared_alt: The Sunken Boat burns to the waterline. Hask swims for the far bank and is met on it.
The narrows are cleared of hull and of Hask. The barges move.
The wreck is dragged out. The river runs and the holds keep their cargo.
Hask takes to the water and does not come out of it. The narrows are open.

bandit_camps.name: Blackbrier Hide
bandit_camps.appears: Iver Cutgrass has cut a camp into the blackbrier where no horse can follow.
bandit_camps.while: Foot traffic on the south track is robbed; the smaller traders stop coming at all.
bandit_camps.cleared: Blackbrier Hide is burned out. The south track carries packs again.
appears_alt: Iver Cutgrass has cut a camp into the blackbrier where no horse can follow.
There are paths cut in the blackbrier that no shepherd made. Iver Cutgrass.
A packman came in with a cut strap and no pack. Iver holds the blackbrier.
Blackbrier Hide is occupied again, and the thorns are on Iver's side.
while_alt: Foot traffic on the south track is robbed; the smaller traders stop coming at all.
Packmen are stripped on the south track. The small trade dries up.
The south track is walked only by Iver's crew - the little traders stay home.
Every pack on the south track is Iver's. The small sellers stop arriving.
cleared_alt: Blackbrier Hide is burned out. The south track carries packs again.
Iver Cutgrass is pulled out of the thorns. The packmen come back.
The blackbrier is cut to the root. The south track is safe on foot.
Iver's paths are burned shut. The small traders fill the market again.

bandit_camps.name: The Charcoal Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Mother Soot and her burners hold the charcoal stands above the wood.
bandit_camps.while: Charcoal runs short; the forge works half days and smith prices climb.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Charcoal Camp is taken. The forge burns a full day again.
appears_alt: Mother Soot and her burners hold the charcoal stands above the wood.
The charcoal stands are smoking for somebody else. Mother Soot is up there.
No charcoal came down the wood road. Mother Soot holds the stands.
Mother Soot is back in the burns, and the smoke is hers now.
while_alt: Charcoal runs short; the forge works half days and smith prices climb.
The forge banks its fire by noon - half a day's work, and the smith's price up.
No charcoal, no heat. The forge shuts early and charges more for what it finishes.
Charcoal comes in by the sack instead of the cart. Half days at the forge, dearer iron.
cleared_alt: The Charcoal Camp is taken. The forge burns a full day again.
Mother Soot is put out. The charcoal carts come down the wood road.
The stands are the town's again - full days at the forge and an honest price.
Mother Soot's burners scatter. The forge keeps its fire till dark.

bandit_camps.name: The Rook Field
bandit_camps.appears: Carrow Dace has set his crew in the rook field, where the crop stands tall enough to hide a man.
bandit_camps.while: Harvest carts are stopped at the field edge; grain comes in short at the measure.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Rook Field is cut early and cleared. The measure fills honestly again.
appears_alt: Carrow Dace has set his crew in the rook field, where the crop stands tall enough to hide a man.
The rook field is full of more than crop. Carrow Dace is in it.
A harvest cart was stopped at the field edge by men who came out of the wheat. Carrow Dace.
There are paths trodden through the rook field that lead nowhere good. Carrow Dace holds it.
while_alt: Harvest carts are stopped at the field edge; grain comes in short at the measure.
The carts are bled at the field edge. The measure never fills.
Grain goes into the rook field and not out of it. The measure reads short.
Carrow takes his share off the cart. The granary counts the difference.
cleared_alt: The Rook Field is cut early and cleared. The measure fills honestly again.
Carrow Dace is flushed out of the wheat. The harvest comes in whole.
The rook field is stubble and no shelter. The measure reads true.
Carrow's crew are cut down with the crop. Grain arrives full weight.

bandit_camps.name: The Salt Road Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Tam Pell has taken the salt road where it narrows, and charges the narrow part.
bandit_camps.while: Salt and cured stores arrive dear; preserved food in town spoils faster for want of it.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Salt Road Camp is broken. Salt comes in at the old price.
appears_alt: Tam Pell has taken the salt road where it narrows, and charges the narrow part.
The salt road has a price on it now. Tam Pell set it.
Salt came in at twice the money. Tam Pell holds the narrows.
Tam Pell is camped where the salt road pinches, and nothing passes cheap.
while_alt: Salt and cured stores arrive dear; preserved food in town spoils faster for want of it.
Salt costs double. What the town cures does not keep.
Dear salt, thin curing - the stores turn before they are eaten.
Tam's price is on every barrel of salt. The preserved food goes off early.
cleared_alt: The Salt Road Camp is broken. Salt comes in at the old price.
Tam Pell is taken off the narrows. The curing sheds are busy again.
The salt road is free. The stores keep their weight and their season.
Tam Pell charges nobody now. Salt is salt-priced.

bandit_camps.name: The Beekeeper's Hut
bandit_camps.appears: Hollis Grin has turned the beekeeper out of his own hut and kept the bees.
bandit_camps.while: Honey, wax and candle stock dry up; the apothecary brews slower without wax.
bandit_camps.cleared: Hollis Grin is stung out of the hut. The beekeeper goes back to his bees.
appears_alt: Hollis Grin has turned the beekeeper out of his own hut and kept the bees.
The beekeeper is in town with nothing but stings. Hollis Grin has his hut.
Hollis Grin is in the hives, and he is not asking the bees.
No wax, no honey, and a grinning man up at the hut. Hollis Grin.
while_alt: Honey, wax and candle stock dry up; the apothecary brews slower without wax.
No wax in town - candles run out and the apothecary's work slows.
Honey and wax both stop. Candles get scarce and the brews take longer.
The hives feed Hollis. Candle stock empties and the apothecary waits on wax.
cleared_alt: Hollis Grin is stung out of the hut. The beekeeper goes back to his bees.
The hut is handed back. Wax, honey and candles come down again.
Hollis Grin leaves swollen and empty-handed. The apothecary gets her wax.
The bees keep their keeper. Candle stock fills the shelf.

bandit_camps.name: The Dry Ferry
bandit_camps.appears: Nils Odd has taken the old ferry landing upriver and runs his own crossing at his own rates.
bandit_camps.while: Half the river trade goes around Bellmire entirely; the Ford takes less each day.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Dry Ferry is sunk at its moorings. The river comes back to the Ford.
appears_alt: Nils Odd has taken the old ferry landing upriver and runs his own crossing at his own rates.
There is a ferry working upriver that nobody chartered. Nils Odd.
Half the river traffic is turning off above the Ford. Nils Odd is why.
Nils Odd has the dry ferry running again, and Bellmire is not on the route.
while_alt: Half the river trade goes around Bellmire entirely; the Ford takes less each day.
The trade crosses upriver now. The Ford's day is quieter and poorer.
Nils takes the crossings Bellmire used to. The Ford's take falls daily.
Half the river never reaches the Ford. The takings drop while the Dry Ferry runs.
cleared_alt: The Dry Ferry is sunk at its moorings. The river comes back to the Ford.
Nils Odd's crossing is cut loose and let go downstream. The Ford is busy again.
The upriver landing is broken up. Every crossing is Bellmire's.
Nils Odd ferries nothing further. The river trade returns to the Ford.

bandit_camps.name: The Ox Road Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Bram Sallow holds the ox road and takes a beast from every team that passes.
bandit_camps.while: Hauling costs double; stone, timber and grain all arrive late and dear.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Ox Road Camp is cleared out. The teams come in whole.
appears_alt: Bram Sallow holds the ox road and takes a beast from every team that passes.
The teams are coming in short an ox apiece. Bram Sallow holds the ox road.
Bram Sallow is camped on the ox road, and his herd grows a head a day.
A hauler walked in leading nothing. Bram Sallow has the ox road.
while_alt: Hauling costs double; stone, timber and grain all arrive late and dear.
Every load costs twice to move. Stone, timber and grain all come in late.
Teams come in a beast short, so everything hauled is slower and dearer.
The hauliers charge double to risk the ox road - and what they carry arrives late.
cleared_alt: The Ox Road Camp is cleared out. The teams come in whole.
Bram Sallow's herd is given back. Hauling costs what it should.
The ox road is safe for a team again. Stone, timber and grain arrive on time.
Bram Sallow walks where he once rode. The teams pass whole and cheap.

monster_camps.name: The Bone Field
monster_camps.appears: Something below spat up its dead, and they are gathering in the north field.
monster_camps.while: The dead multiply nightly and gnaw at the outlying farms.
monster_camps.cleared: The Bone Field is put down. The north field is only a field again.
appears_alt: Something below spat up its dead again, and they are gathering in the north field.
The north field is standing up. The Bone Field is open.
The dead are walking in from the north field, and there are more each night.
The scar gave back its dead. They have chosen the north field.
while_alt: The dead multiply nightly and gnaw at the outlying farms.
More of them every night, and the outlying farms take the bites.
The field breeds dead; the farms on the edge pay for it in the dark.
Their number grows each night, and the far farms are chewed at.
cleared_alt: The Bone Field is put down. The north field is only a field again.
The last of them is laid flat. The north field grows crop, not corpses.
The Bone Field is burned and turned. The farms sleep whole.
Nothing stands in the north field but stubble.

monster_camps.name: The Slime Warren
monster_camps.appears: A slime nest has taken the old quarry, and it doubles every night it is left alone.
monster_camps.while: The quarry is lost, and the nest creeps toward the homes.
monster_camps.cleared: The Slime Warren is burned out. The quarry stops twitching.
appears_alt: A slime nest has taken the old quarry, and it doubles every night it is left alone.
The old quarry is full and moving. The Slime Warren is back.
Something boiled up in the quarry floor overnight, and it is twice the size by morning.
The quarry has gone soft underfoot. A warren is in it.
while_alt: The quarry is lost, and the nest creeps toward the homes.
No work in the quarry, and the nest edges nearer the houses each night.
The quarry belongs to the nest, and the nest is coming downhill.
The quarry is given up, and whatever is in it is heading for the doors.
cleared_alt: The Slime Warren is burned out. The quarry stops twitching.
The quarry is scoured clean. Nothing in it moves on its own.
The warren is boiled off. The quarry is stone again.
The Slime Warren is finished. The quarry floor holds still.

monster_camps.name: The Belltower Roost
monster_camps.appears: A roost of cave bats has taken the bell-tower; they foul the wells and spook every horse in town.
monster_camps.while: The wells need watching, and the beasts are restless while they hang there.
monster_camps.cleared: The Roost is cleared. The bell-tower is quiet. Almost.
appears_alt: A roost of cave bats has taken the bell-tower again; they foul the wells and spook every horse in town.
The bell-tower is black with wings. The Roost is back.
Something came up out of the scar and hung itself in the bell-tower.
The bell will not ring for the things in it. Cave bats have the tower.
while_alt: The wells need watching, and the beasts are restless while they hang there.
Every well is guarded and skimmed; the horses will not settle while the tower hangs full.
The wells are fouled faster than they are drawn, and no animal in town sleeps.
Watchmen on the wells, and not a quiet beast in the stables.
cleared_alt: The Roost is cleared. The bell-tower is quiet. Almost.
The bell-tower is emptied out. The wells run clean and the horses stand easy.
The wings are gone off the tower. The bell is rung to prove it.
The Belltower Roost is cleared. The wells are drawn without a skimmer.

monster_camps.name: The Sedge Mound
monster_camps.appears: The fen has gone loud - bog frogs the size of dogs have mounded up in the sedge.
monster_camps.while: The fen path is lost, and the fishers work the river or not at all.
monster_camps.cleared: The Sedge Mound is cleared. The fen is merely unpleasant again.
appears_alt: The fen has gone loud again - bog frogs the size of dogs have mounded up in the sedge.
Something is calling out of the sedge all night, and it is not a bird.
The Sedge Mound is up, and the fen path is not worth walking.
Bog frogs have piled into the sedge, and they are the wrong size for frogs.
while_alt: The fen path is lost, and the fishers work the river or not at all.
Nobody takes the fen path; the fishers crowd the river or stay ashore.
The fen is given up. Fishing is river-only, and thinner for it.
The path through the fen is closed. The catch comes off the river or nowhere.
cleared_alt: The Sedge Mound is cleared. The fen is merely unpleasant again.
The sedge is quiet. The fen path carries fishers.
The mound is broken up. The fen is back to mud and midges.
The Sedge Mound is finished. The fen path is walkable.

monster_camps.name: The Silk Barn
monster_camps.appears: A barn on the south road has gone white - cave spiders came up out of the scar and took it.
monster_camps.while: The south road is spun shut; nothing moves past the barn after dusk.
monster_camps.cleared: The Silk Barn burns. The south road is clear, and nothing is watching it.
appears_alt: A barn on the south road has gone white again - cave spiders came up out of the scar and took it.
The south road's barn is wrapped to the rafters. Something took it in the night.
There is silk across the south road, and a barn behind it that nobody will open.
Cave spiders have the barn on the south road. It is white from the gate.
while_alt: The south road is spun shut; nothing moves past the barn after dusk.
The silk closes the south road at dusk - no cart, no rider, no pack.
After dark the south road is webbed over, and nothing passes the barn.
The barn seals the south road each night. Nothing gets by it.
cleared_alt: The Silk Barn burns. The south road is clear, and nothing is watching it.
The barn is burned to the sill. The south road runs after dark.
The silk is fired off the south road. The barn is only a ruin.
The Silk Barn is cleared. Nothing hangs over the south road.

monster_camps.name: The Gnaw Pits
monster_camps.appears: Scar rats have got into the old root pits, and they are not the size rats are meant to be.
monster_camps.while: Stores are gnawed through nightly; what the town keeps, it keeps losing.
monster_camps.cleared: The Gnaw Pits are flooded out. The stores hold their weight overnight again.
appears_alt: Scar rats have got into the old root pits again, and they are not the size rats are meant to be.
The root pits are moving. Scar rats are in them.
Something the wrong size for a rat went into the root pits, and brought family.
The Gnaw Pits are busy again, and the stores are showing it.
while_alt: Stores are gnawed through nightly; what the town keeps, it keeps losing.
The stores lose a little every night. Nothing the town saves stays saved.
Sacks are opened from below each night; the stores run down on their own.
Whatever is put by is gnawed through by morning.
cleared_alt: The Gnaw Pits are flooded out. The stores hold their weight overnight again.
The root pits are drowned and dug over. The sacks stay shut.
The Gnaw Pits are cleared. What the town stores, it keeps.
The pits are emptied and limed. The stores stop shrinking.

monster_camps.name: The Drowned Pen
monster_camps.appears: Something came up the flooded ditch and has settled in the stock pen at the water's edge.
monster_camps.while: Livestock go a head a night, and the herds will not drink near the water.
monster_camps.cleared: The Drowned Pen is cleared and the ditch dug out. The herds drink again.
appears_alt: Something came up the flooded ditch again and has settled in the stock pen at the water's edge.
The Drowned Pen has a tenant. It came up the ditch.
There is something in the waterside pen that was not bought at market.
The flooded ditch brought something up, and it likes the stock pen.
while_alt: Livestock go a head a night, and the herds will not drink near the water.
A beast a night out of the pen, and nothing will take water at the ditch.
The herds lose one a night and refuse the waterside entirely.
Stock vanishes nightly from the pen; the rest will not drink there at all.
cleared_alt: The Drowned Pen is cleared and the ditch dug out. The herds drink again.
Whatever came up the ditch goes back down it in pieces. The pen is safe.
The waterside pen is cleared. The stock drink where they always did.
The Drowned Pen holds beasts and nothing else. The herds settle.

monster_camps.name: The Candle Wood
monster_camps.appears: Lights have taken the coppice east of town, and they walk the paths at dusk like a procession.
monster_camps.while: The woodcutters refuse the coppice; firewood and charcoal run short in town.
monster_camps.cleared: The Candle Wood goes dark. The cutters go back in by daylight, then by dusk.
appears_alt: Lights have taken the coppice east of town again, and they walk the paths at dusk like a procession.
The east coppice is lit and nobody lit it. The Candle Wood is back.
There are lamps among the trees that move when you look away.
Scar wisps are in the coppice, walking the cut paths in file.
while_alt: The woodcutters refuse the coppice; firewood and charcoal run short in town.
No cutter goes east. Firewood thins and charcoal with it.
The coppice is left standing - and the wood piles in town go down.
The cutters will not work the lights. Fuel runs short on both counts.
cleared_alt: The Candle Wood goes dark. The cutters go back in by daylight, then by dusk.
The lights are put out. The coppice is cut again.
The Candle Wood is cleared. Firewood and charcoal come down the east road.
Nothing walks the coppice paths. The cutters work it to dusk.

monster_camps.name: The Kiln Nest
monster_camps.appears: Fire beetles have bored into the brick kiln and glow in its mouth all night.
monster_camps.while: The kiln cannot be fired; brick, tile and pottery all stop at once.
monster_camps.cleared: The Kiln Nest is smoked out. The kiln fires clean, and the tiles come again.
appears_alt: Fire beetles have bored into the brick kiln again and glow in its mouth all night.
The kiln is lit and nobody lit it. Something is living in the heat.
There are coals in the kiln mouth that crawl. Fire beetles.
The Kiln Nest is back - the kiln glows all night and fires nothing.
while_alt: The kiln cannot be fired; brick, tile and pottery all stop at once.
No firing while they nest in it - brick, tile and pot all stop together.
The kiln is theirs. Brickwork, roofing and crockery all halt.
Nothing can be fired. Brick, tile and pottery dry out unfinished.
cleared_alt: The Kiln Nest is smoked out. The kiln fires clean, and the tiles come again.
The beetles are driven out of the brickwork. The kiln takes a proper load.
The Kiln Nest is cleared. Brick, tile and pot all move again.
The kiln is swept and lit by hand. The tiles stack up.

monster_camps.name: Gibbet Hill
monster_camps.appears: The hanged have got up off Gibbet Hill, and they keep to the road they knew.
monster_camps.while: The north road belongs to the dead after dark; nothing travels it and the post stops.
monster_camps.cleared: Gibbet Hill is put down and the ground turned. The road is only a road.
appears_alt: The hanged have got up off Gibbet Hill again, and they keep to the road they knew.
Gibbet Hill is empty of ropes and full of walking. They are on the north road.
The gibbets are swinging light tonight. Their tenants are on the road.
The hanged have come down off the hill, and they remember the way to town.
while_alt: The north road belongs to the dead after dark; nothing travels it and the post stops.
After dusk the north road is theirs. No traveller, no post.
Nothing goes up the north road at night. The letters pile up unsent.
The dead hold the north road from dusk. The post does not run.
cleared_alt: Gibbet Hill is put down and the ground turned. The road is only a road.
The hanged are laid down for good. The north road carries the post.
Gibbet Hill is cleared and limed. The road runs after dark.
They go back under the hill. The north road is travelled again.

monster_camps.name: The Granary Swarm
monster_camps.appears: A nest the size of a cart hangs in the granary roof, and this is not the season for it.
monster_camps.while: The granary cannot be worked; stored grain spoils where it stands.
monster_camps.cleared: The Granary Swarm is burned out. The grain is turned, and most of it is saved.
appears_alt: A nest the size of a cart hangs in the granary roof again, and this is not the season for it.
The granary roof is humming. Something built in it overnight.
Scar wasps have hung a nest in the granary, and it is bigger than a man.
Nobody will go into the granary. There is a nest in the rafters the size of a cart.
while_alt: The granary cannot be worked; stored grain spoils where it stands.
The granary stands shut - the grain in it turns untouched.
No hand goes into the granary. The stored grain goes off on the floor.
The grain cannot be turned or drawn. It spoils where it lies.
cleared_alt: The Granary Swarm is burned out. The grain is turned, and most of it is saved.
The nest comes down in smoke. The granary is worked again.
The Granary Swarm is cleared. The grain is turned before it goes.
The rafters are empty. The granary opens and most of the grain is good.

monster_camps.name: The Stone Yard
monster_camps.appears: Two things out of the deep have taken the mason's yard and are eating the mortar.
monster_camps.while: Cut stone and finished work are wrecked nightly; every build in town slows.
monster_camps.cleared: The Stone Yard is retaken. The masons find their tools, and a troll's tooth in a block.
appears_alt: Two things out of the deep have taken the mason's yard again and are eating the mortar.
The mason's yard has visitors that chew stone. Something came up for it.
There are footprints in the mason's yard a hand deep. Cave trolls.
Something is eating the mortar in the stone yard, and it brought a friend.
while_alt: Cut stone and finished work are wrecked nightly; every build in town slows.
Dressed stone is smashed each night; everything being built slows to a crawl.
The yard's work is ruined by morning. Every build in town falls behind.
Finished stone is broken nightly. Nothing in town rises on time.
cleared_alt: The Stone Yard is retaken. The masons find their tools, and a troll's tooth in a block.
The yard is cleared. The dressed stone survives the night.
The Stone Yard is the masons' again. The builds pick up.
Both of them are put down in the yard. The stone stays cut.

monster_camps.name: The Thornwake
monster_camps.appears: Something hound-shaped dens in the thornwake, and it hunts in a pack now.
monster_camps.while: Flocks and herds are taken nightly; the pens empty and the drovers will not go out.
monster_camps.cleared: The Thornwake is cleared. The flocks sleep out again.
appears_alt: Something hound-shaped dens in the thornwake again, and it hunts in a pack now.
The thornwake has a den in it, and the den has grown.
There are hounds in the thornwake that no one bred.
The Thornwake is denned again, and the pack is bigger this time.
while_alt: Flocks and herds are taken nightly; the pens empty and the drovers will not go out.
A loss every night out of the pens, and no drover will walk the road.
The flocks thin by the night. The pens stand half-empty and the drovers stay in.
Herds and flocks are taken each night; nobody will drive them anywhere.
cleared_alt: The Thornwake is cleared. The flocks sleep out again.
The den is dug out and burned. The drovers take the road.
The Thornwake is emptied. The pens fill and stay full.
The pack is put down in the thorns. The flocks are left alone.

monster_camps.name: The Reed Hollow

events._note_variants_c24: Widened C-cycle 24: wandering_boss appears_alt / while_alt / cleared_alt 6 -> 14 each. There is still only one wandering boss, so these three are the lines that repeat most. Every while_alt states the same implementable cost as the canonical while - one outlying holding razed per day it roams, and the dark it drags persists on the ruin. name, appears, while, cleared and note are UNCHANGED. Additive; dead until wired.
events._note_variants_c29: Widened C-cycle 29: every bandit camp (20) and every monster camp (19) now carries appears_alt / while_alt / cleared_alt - 4 lines each, the same key shape wandering_boss already uses. Each camp previously had exactly ONE appears, while and cleared line, so the second time the same camp spawned on a stream it read word for word. Each while_alt states the SAME implementable cost as that camp's canonical `while` - reworded, never widened: no alt adds an effect the canonical line does not already state, so the desktop worker can implement the cost once per camp and pick any line to show. name, leader, of, appears, while and cleared are UNCHANGED on every camp. No new camp, no new named leader. Additive; dead until wired.

growth_tiers._note: Town growth stages (D31/D32) - the town levels far too fast, so this is a long, earned climb. For each: the stage name, the crier's line on reaching it, and what a viewer should SEE appear. Complements town_levels_for_the_desktop (coarser, 7 levels). Dead until wired.

tiers.name: Crossing
tiers.crier: A handful of huts at a river crossing. Somebody calls it Bellmire.
tiers.see: Three or four huts, a cart, a cookfire.

tiers.name: Hamlet
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a hamlet now - a well dug, and a reason to stay.
tiers.see: A well, a few more homes, a fenced garden or two.

tiers.name: The Guild Post
tiers.crier: The guild plants a post at Bellmire. The post has a door, and the door is kept.
tiers.see: The guild post building, and the town's first lamp.

tiers.name: Village
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a village. The scar has a name, and so do we.
tiers.see: Homes clustered along a cart-track, chickens, a shared pen.

tiers.name: Market Day
tiers.crier: Market day comes to Bellmire. Measure the grain.
tiers.see: A market square with a few stalls, and the first outside traders.

tiers.name: The Chapel
tiers.crier: A chapel and a bell-tower rise. The bell has no clapper, and rings anyway.
tiers.see: The temple and its tower, and a small graveyard behind it.

tiers.name: Craft Row
tiers.crier: The smiths and masons raise Craft Row. Count the flasks.
tiers.see: Workshops trailing smoke, a forge-glow, the mill wheel turning.

tiers.name: The Garrison
tiers.crier: Bellmire raises a garrison. The guard has a yard now - and a Commander.
tiers.see: Barracks and a training yard, guards on patrol, E3PO up on the wall.

tiers.name: Market Town
tiers.crier: Bellmire stands as a proper market town. The caravans know the road.
tiers.see: A paved square, more districts, a busy Ford with its Ferryman.

tiers.name: The First Wall
tiers.crier: Stone goes up where the fields used to stop. Keep the door.
tiers.see: A low wall around the town's heart, and a gatehouse over the road.

tiers.name: Walled Town
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a walled town now. Let them come.
tiers.see: A full curtain wall, corner towers, a district banner on each quarter.

tiers.name: City in all but Charter
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a city in all but the charter - and the scar is deeper than it has ever been.
tiers.see: Dense districts, a second ring of homes outside the wall, traffic at every gate.
